Title: Mr. Nobody Against Putin
Review: Powerful documentary which manages to show us a peek inside of how Russian war propaganda is used to indoctrinate the children, but also how the most polluted town in the world is more than just an ugly stat, namely also a vibrant and beautiful community. Pavel is a heroic teacher and I'm thankful for this work.

Title: Todo sobre mi madre
Review: Great, creative storytelling and script, captivating actors in a remarkable and applaudable mix of hard-hitting drama and playful comedy. The production is gorgeous: vivid colors, good use of music. This one really surprised me, there's much to appreciate here. Very good film.

Title: Paul Blart: Mall Cop 2
Review: I know it's just a simple mainstream comedy, but who decided to make Paul Blart such an asshole in the first half of the film? Not cool.

Title: Paul Blart: Mall Cop
Review: Not a very good film but did make me laugh at times. Somewhat enjoyable.

Title: Spaceballs
Review: Not a great fan of Brooks, but plenty of funny moments and I applaud the effort.

Title: Winter Sleep
Review: This is a great film. The combination of its psychological complexity and moral ambiguity, and its breath-taking photography and cinematography in general make this feel like an modern Ingmar Bergman epic. The one thing keeping this from being 5/5 for me is the somewhat overtly theatrical, dramatic touch. Sometimes the dialogues seem to almost cross the fourth wall, tainting some of the realism that helps make this film so great. Nonetheless, this is a beautiful film.

Title: Viridiana
Review: What a powerful blow to optimism, delivered in the entertaining form of absurd comedy like Buñuel does so well. Piety seems to be depicted as naive, so much so that I wonder how Viridiana's faith will hold up. I loved the dark twist with the increasingly derailing dinner scene at the end. Good film.

Title: Een vrouw onder invloed
Review: Mostly through the phenomenal acting by Peter Falke and especially Gena Rowlands. this film manages to reach great depth with a straightforward plot and minimal - but very powerful - script. Without being mentioned explicitly, topics that come up include how to regard and treat people with mental illness, how the mother-child relation is affected by this, as well as how it affects the love experienced between husband and wife. Near the end when Mabel asks Nick whether he loves her, and he struggles only to eventually avoid saying yes is where the film wraps things up perfectly. Great film!

Title: Arrival
Review: A very brave and well-done adaptation of Ted Chiang's short story, which strikes me as a very hard thing to do well, the theme and writing being so abstract and intellectual in nature. Yet, Villeneuve managed to do a good job, including making it more accessible - albeit at the sacrifice of some depth - to the general public. His signature style of drone-heavy ambient, minimalist CGI and beautiful photography really made this into a beauty of a film.

Title: The Wicker Man
Review: A playful, fun but still thought-provoking film. The Summer Isle community is a wonderfully fantasized place, and it truly climaxes with the May day and its absurdity and costumes.

Title: Titane
Review: While curiously awaiting the fruits of what may perhaps be the most curious pregnancy I have ever borne withess to, TITANE manages to entertain with its erotic, futuristic style. The film elevates sheer entertainmant in its second half, when Alexia develops a son-father bond with the fire fighters captain. I really love his acting and the absurdity of their trauma-induced relationship. Very interesting film.

Title: Ace Ventura: When Nature Calls
Review: Otherwise cliche Hollywood worth your while thanks to Jim's gift!

Title: The Thirteenth Floor
Review: A cliche Hollywood disgrace to the book.

Title: The Substance
Review: One of the most gory body horrors I've ever seen, but with substance! The societal critique on the sexualization of women is obvious, but using this genre to shape the attack is really cool. This film shares its eeriness with films such as Being John Malkovich and Amer, but also reminds of the tongue-in-cheek Spring Breakers. The ultraslick style isn't always my taste, but it is done with care and consistency. This is a good watch.

Title: The Brutalist
Review: Such an ambitious piece. Reminding me of 70s US cinema , this slow-paced, visually stunning epic is just a must-see. How it manages to have history, art and the psychological toll of greatness intertwine in such an audio-visual film is a great achievement. Fantastic acting, a wonderfully supporting soundtrack and above all breath-taking photography and camera work. Try to catch this on a big screen!

Title: Liar Liar
Review: Jim Carrey's gift turns this otherwise cliche Hollywood film into a great time. Don't expect a good film, but a good laugh, and this is certainly worthwile.

Title: The Adventures of Prince Achmed
Review: Such creativity in the early days of film. Her techniques for adding depth are stunning. The comical style of depiction and movement really fits the Arabic setting well, and each of the manually drawn frames are filled with Reiniger's passion. To top it all off I was lucky enough to have seen this with live music played on top of it composed by Steven Kamperman. It was a marvelous experience.

Title: How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies
Review: I'm not crazy about comedy dramas: the genres just don't seem to work well together. Characters just never feel quite real, and there's an annoying comedic touch in the acting that disbalances the good acting in the dramatic scenes. Overall though the film is a nice watch. Grandma is great and the film conveys its lesson well. My favorite thing, by the way, might be the exceptional tailored piano soundtrack.

Title: The Kings of the World
Review: Those who have nothing, have nothing to lose. A beautiful depiction of the raw lives of these youngsters from the streets of Colombia. The bipolar nature of the film makes you live through the youthful, playful highs as well as the terrifying, crippling lows. The dreamy, surrealistic touch really finishes it off. Great film.

Title: So Long, My Son
Review: Great stories do much of the storytelling themselves, you just have to know how to present it interestingly. Just showing, rather than obtrusively telling, relying on the great acting, beautiful shots, raw and ambiguous characters and plentifulness of runtime, this film is a true work of art.

Title: A Million Ways to Die in the West
Review: Mostly cliche, but has a few enjoyable jokes.

Title: Ace Ventura: Pet Detective
Review: Much of this film sadly is horribly mainstream Hollywood, but Jim Carrey's exceptional talent completely makes up for this. Once he gets rolling, it's simply a comedic virtuoso. As hard as he's made me laugh, this film feels like a weird combination of a standard Hollywood cliche, and a comedy masterpiece. Definitely recommended.

Title: Decision to Leave
Review: This is a film of great craftmanship. An interesting romance to start with, lending itself for an interesting plot development. The dreamy sequences and guesswork left to the viewer makes it a fun watch. The complexity is admirable. Aesthetically there's a lot to be enjoyed as well: there certainly are quite some very interesting shots to admire. What does put me of, however, is the cartoony feel and oversaturated colors. It aided the somewhat theatrical style that I'm simply not a fan of. Great film, but with some mismatches with my taste.

Title: The Long Good Friday
Review: Well-crafted film that balances entertainment with cinematic aesthetics very well. The fantastic soundtrack, goofy acting, oddball humor and careful caricatures all add up to a great style. The story is interesting as well. If I had to point out something negative, it is that I'm not entirely sure about everyone's acting skills. It definitely didn't truly bother me though.

Title: Unruly
Review: Engaging, disturbing and educational about the history of oppression of women. I love how heartfelt the film is at times as wel; it is really well-balanced. The photography is good, the acting is fantastic and there are no cheap shots. Great film!

Title: The Green Butchers
Review: This was an enjoyable film. In many regards it's too mainstream for my taste, but I definitely appreciated a few great dark jokes.

Title: Oppenheimer
Review: Yet another great cinematic experience from the hands of the director who has bridged the gap between mainstream and art. Similarly to INTERSTELLAR, this film is a fantastic audiovisual experience. The story telling is also well done. What I loved in particular is how doubt and moral ambiguity play a central role in the film in various ways. Not only through the first person experience of Oppenheimer, but also through the fourth wall, in the celebratory scenes for example. Other than some sentimental cliches, I really liked this movie.

Title: The Super Mario Bros. Movie
Review: Carefully crafted classic children's movie with tons of creative references to the game franchise. The style is really close to the feeling of the games, even including the subtle use of some in-game music classics. I also think the way the original identity of the Mario bros. as Italian plumbers from Brooklyn has been combined very successfully with the in-game world and identity. The humor is good, for children in particular but also for adults it's absolutely enjoyable. All in all this is a fun watch, very well balanced, creative and nostalgic.

Title: The Lighthouse
Review: Fantastic experience. The photography is superb from the first shot to the last. Great and varied composition, interesting use of shadow and an interesting choice for an 4:3 aspect ratio, which gives the film a more claustrophobic feel. The humor is fantastic, and the subtle psychological horror surrounding the mystical lighthouse (or working with it, rather) is simple but remains interesting throughout. For my taste, the film could've been more slowly paced, but that's an extravagant preference I guess. Great film!

Title: Clue
Review: This film is great fun in all sorts of ways with its scripted jokes, bizarre slapstick-esque hysteria and subtle moments of absurdity. It does lose a little of its shine over time, but that's made up for by the incredible ending, which is both clever, fun and climactic.

Title: My Führer
Review: It's a neat idea, and the utterly fragile Hitler has definitely made me laugh. However, much about the film is just too cliche too really get excited about it. Still, it's a fun watch for a lazy day.

Title: Sisters with Transistors
Review: A great piece on the evolution of avant-garde electronic music from the point of view of some of the women pioneers. We learn about the struggle these women endured, who they are and what drove them towards making this kind of music. What is really well done is how the music is integrated in the documentary to function as its soundtrack. The aesthetics of this film are great all around. Very good watch.

Title: The Human Condition III: A Soldier's Prayer
Review: Coming full circle, after Japan's loss of the war, it is now Kaji who is on the side of the oppressed. After a final spurt of energy, he finally surrenders and gets placed in a work camp, just like the one he used to lead himself. It is here where his final hope in humanity is tested: his hope in the socialist Russians. The truth is bitter.

Title: The Human Condition II: Road to Eternity
Review: Kaji's rough struggle to do good increasingly makes him pay the price. His admirable character seems to always find his way up ranks, but he just never gets quite there. Man's ugly mindset keeps running one step ahead of him, but he does not back down. Again, wartime highlights the ugliness within us, and this time Kaji is right in the middle of it.

Title: The Human Condition
Review: Great film. See my reviews of the three separate releases.

Title: The Human Condition I: No Greater Love
Review: What setting could be more appropriate to make a film about the human condition than that of war? This major source of (ultimately) unnecessary suffering (for all) really highlights what it means to be human. Kaji's rare presence of being a humanist truly provides an interesting contrast with most other people's racist and tribal character, sharpening the lens through which we analyze our species' nature. Great film.

Title: Miller's Crossing
Review: Superbly crafted film. It's just that weird atmosphere, I love it. The dark, gritty photography and fantastic decoration and dressing are amazing. The music, the use of lighting... Aesthetically this is all-round great. The story is complex and interesting, the characters are fun, although I have to say the comical bits had 50/50 hits and misses with me.

Title: Harakiri
Review: An anti-Samurai masterpiece. There's nothing as powerful as a man who has nothing to lose, but great things to tell. Hanshirō's misfortune has put him in a position outside of any cultural frame of reference, a position of pure nihilism, of ultimate reflection. If only the Iyi clanspeople could understand him, but unfortunately they are still trapped in the arbitrary beliefs and empty pride that is the Samurai code.

Title: De dag waarop de aarde stilstond
Review: Incredible feat for a 1951 film. The core idea is very solid, and the deeper message for all humanity has been conveyed through the fourth wall. I didn't care much for the drama side of the film, with its hints of romance. Also, I found myself -unusually so- annoyed at sloppy details regarding the disabling of electricity. There's lots to love, but I feel 50s Hollywood has held back the potential of this film.

Title: Ontleding van een moord
Review: Who would ever have thought I'd almost cheer for a lawyer who deploys sleezy tricks and rhetoric. Perhaps had I known it'd be James Stewart, it would've been different. I loved the slow pace and realism, where every last detail seemed thought of. Well executed film that is interesting from start to end.

Title: M
Review: An absolute masterpiece. It's truly amazing how progressive this film is. It could honestly almost pass for a (great) film from the 60s, if not 70s. Its plot is clever and creative, and the film really captivates you. The use of camera and photography is stunning, and the genre a brilliant mix of moral tale and inventive crime. To top it off, there's atruly climactic and brave ending. Wonderful film.

Title: De onzichtbare man
Review: I'm a big fan of H.G. Wells and I was a little skeptical to see how this film would represent his book. Gladly, it was the great James Whale who took on the job, and he accomplished it very nicely. To think that this was done in the 30s is very impressive. I really wish the romance part in these films wasn't so emphasized, but other than that this was a good film.

Title: Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill!
Review: This film has that cult quality where cheap ingredients somehow yield a great dish. It's hard to explain and quite surprising, but ultimately this manages to be fun, over-the-top enjoyable and it even has a good story arch. As in: I didn't get bored with it as I often do with some parts in cult films. All in all really enjoyable, but let's not get carried away either.

Title: Dead Times
Review: Everything by Laloux is great, but I didn't see this cynical, (potentially unintentionally) comical, misanthropic side of his yet. The drawing is amazing as always, and the theme unusually (for him) realistic and dreadful. A great 10 minutes in my life.

Title: Vinni-Pukh and a Busy Day
Review: Clever, and this time with a nice rendition of Eeyore the donkey. Also, I can't get enough of these beautiful drawings.

Title: Vinni-Pukh Goes Visiting
Review: The humor in this one really takes off. Very funny stuff, timeless!

Title: Vinni-Pukh
Review: The drawings are beautiful, and the characters fun. The "simple philosopher" character of Vinni Pukh, the dry humor: lovely!

Title: The Fly
Review: The evolving gore alone is worth the watch, but man this film has a lot more to offer. The sci-fi idea is so simple, yet who on Earth isn't captivated by this thought experiment? The attention for angst and psychological suffering really takes this film to a deeper level. And seriously, sometimes the line between absurd comedy and genuine moral horror was very thin. Great film.

Title: Troll 2
Review: Sometimes I can enjoy a bad film that's just really, really bad. But if it's just bad enough, realy too bad, you're gonna have a bad time. Didn't watch beyond the first half hour. Completely unenjoyable.

Title: The Big Short
Review: This film was a nice surprise. I feared a Hollywood cliche with good information in it, but actually found a good film allround. Kudos to Steve Carell in particular: I didn't know he had this in him.

Title: The Long Goodbye
Review:
The Long Goodbye

It takes Altman to understand a genre and abuse it friendly. I just love how this film entertains you by laughing at itself, it's just so fresh. Gould plays his part perfectly and as always there's this subtle layer of surreal goofiness that I can somehow stand only when Altman does it. Fantastic film that keeps you interested in many ways during every second of it.

Title: Before Midnight
Review: A fitting part in the trilogy, although a bit of a let down. The emphasis on sexuality and gender often felt annoying and unnecessary, and I felt very aware of the fourth wall from time to time. I do wonder if the annoyance I felt was intentional, as a realistic display of what life turns us into when we get older, but still, I'm left with an impression of sloppiness at least. Still it's a nice finale of the trilogy.

Title: Frankenstein
Review: This was surprisingly good. There was some real attention for lots of cinematographic detail, some shots were simply stunning. The creation scene was incredible, and I admire the enthralling story arch which peaked in the mob going after "the monster". Finally there's a moral lesson to appreciate: there's no such thing as a criminal brain.

Title: Frankenstein
Review: Interesting from a historical perspective to say the least, this short film is certainly something special. It's hard for it to fully captivate me being so dated and technologically limited, but the scene where Frankenstein comes to life from the fire definitely stood out for me. Altogether I respect it, but it's hard to get too excited about.

Title: Crack: Cocaine, Corruption & Conspiracy
Review: Not being from the US myself, even though I'm superficially familiar with this bit of history, the specifics to do with how government "combatted" these issues resembled the depiction in the series "The Wire" to a scary degree. Very important information that should convince every last skeptic when it comes to racial injustice in the US.

Title: Riders of Justice
Review: This film had qualities, but failed to calibrate the whole nicely. It's too explicit and agressive for young children, but too childish for an adult audience at the same time. The nerd characterization was fun at times, but also over the top. On top of it all it was super unrealistic, to the extent where it got annoying. I can enjoy a dark revenge film, but this one was mostly disappointing.

Title: Blade Runner 2049
Review: This film took me by surprise. Such an incredible style! A clean sort of cyberpunk, darkness with bright colors on top, and accompanying drone music and Vangelis-like synths respectively. I am fairly disappointed with the cliche acting, characters and plot though. In the hand of a less mainstream director this could have been much better. Still, it's lovely to immerse yourself in this world.

Title: What We Did on Our Holiday
Review: This is a great film for children perhaps, but it took me a while to realize that I could try to watch it that way. Grandpa and the children on the beach has something special, and the message the film conveys is a good one to learn early on: death is part of life, and adults can maybe actually learn something from the innocence of children there. That being said, I can't rate it higher due to the cliche feel.

Title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
Review: I'm not a fan of musicals, but this film's authenticity escapes boundaries like those. Great decors, a unique mix of playful eroticism, sci-fi classics name dropping and, most importantly to me, a strong message championing non-heterosexuals. Despite the qualities, I did struggle to get through some of the songs and humor though.

Title: Midnight Express
Review: Entertaining at best. The acting isn't very good, and much of the story feels rushed and unncessary. The biographical accuracy is poor, and the depiction of the Turkish people is controversial. Oliver Stone actually apologized for this "tampering with the truth". I like the adventurous feel the film has though, and it lends for some interesting moral discussions about prisons, victimhood and justice.

Title: Druk
Review: An ode to this ancient potion of life, but no less a warning against its unwieldy powers. How it seduces us to comfortably remain within its magical enhancement of reality, only to betray us, immersing us in solitary darkness and deconstructed, fragmented reality, and ultimately return us to our now increasingly dreadful, sober reality. That being said though: it's lovely to drink every now and then, right?

Title: Shadows
Review: This film just breaths jazz in every possible way. It is so refreshing and odd, for its time especially. I love how aimless it seems, by which it brings interesting issues of the time -such as feminism and racism- to the viewer in a very natural way, i.e. through improvised acting rather than heavy scripting. This is a rare form of acting to see, but it's lovely, and very goofy and funny as well. I had a great time!

Title: Gisaengchung
Review: At first I enjoyed the absurdity and clever script, with its many extremities which work thanks to the odd style. Dark, psychological humor which peaks in the "drinking in the living room" scene. But then, the basement happens, and a lot of cheap choices are made. Cringy humor, an incoherent twist to the horror genre, lack of aim (randomness) and even more unlikely events occur. It's a nice film, but with its faults.

Title: The Fog
Review: Aesthetically, there's much to praise in this film. Beautifully shot, great use of lighting and bright colors (which seems to be inspired by Giallo), and a cool and very functional soundtrack written by Carpenter himself. However, the story feels really shaky and uninteresting, and something you never really get to care about much. The pacing seems odd as well, and the acting is subpar. Not very good, but enjoyable.

Title: All the President's Men
Review: An entertaining and exciting view into the Watergate scandal, starring a lovable team of Redford and Hoffman. It's all about the suspense and unraveling of the mystery in this film, which is carried by substance, not cheap tricks. It's the details that make a slow paced film like this successful, such as the banter at the office and quality of character of the two protagonists. Very good film.

Title: The Red Turtle
Review: Tranquil, simple, breathtakingly beautiful, but slightly boring. It doesn't entirely succeed in immersing the viewer in the mystery, which has tainted the experience a little. Nonetheless, the story has an appeal, and the esthetics are simply amazing, ultimately making this a good film.

Title: Shaun the Sheep Movie
Review: It's hard to make an animated film stand out for me. They tend to be amusing and nice, but rarely completely horrible or amazing. Shaun the Sheep is definitely a bit more special than that. Besides loving Aardman's animation style, I'm usually put off a bit by the infantile, formulaic storyline. This film, however, stands out because of its incredible details, both in animation as in script. Really nice film!

Title: Fanny and Alexander (Television Version)
Review: This is a great work of art. Bergman manages to utilize many of his signature traits, including the touch of the surreal, intense grieving and psychological drama, and make that work even in such a long film. The long duration benefits immersion greatly and allows for a very good exploration of the psyches of all people involved. Besides being authentically dramatical, it contains great comical scenes as well.

Title: Kitchen Stories
Review: This is a neat little film. It wraps an interesting experiment in an accessible and warm style suitable for a large audience.

Title: Blame!
Review: I did not like much about this film. I struggle to accept many of the anime cliches, and wasn't immersed into the story as much as I would have liked. I mean, the idea is pretty cool. Anyways, the style and technical aspects are all very nice, which made it enjoyable to watch ultimately.

Title: What Did Jack Do?
Review: Great concept and succesfully done. The reference to the genre cliches are clear, and the overall atmosphere works well. Jack's voice is subtly well chosen, as are the things he says. A good balance between absurdity, dark comedy and realism: this is a welcome addition to Lynch's work.

Title: Isle of Dogs
Review: The theatrical style Anderson has developed over the years is not entirely my cup of tea, but for some reason I love it in his animated films. "Fantastic Mr. Fox" was incredible, and this film too was great. The animations are beautiful, the story is touching and inventive, the characters loveable. Suited for children too I would suppose.

Title: Chicken Run
Review: Sadly I'm not a child anymore, because I'm sure this would've been a lot more enjoyable then. It's a fun watch nonetheless. I like the Aardman stop-motion style, and had some good laughs. I also appreciate the animal-friendly perspective of the film. It was fun.

Title: The Game
Review: The film has an entertaining suspense to it, and the increasing paranoia and insanity is enjoyable. I think Douglas acts well and the production of the film is solid. I do think it's all a bit too incredulous for my taste in the end, but it's definitely a nice movie.

Title: Nazarin
Review: Through the lense of cynical, dark, but subtle comedy Buñuel manages to make us laugh at his portrayal of humanity, which, sadly, is a vivid reflection of reality. The well-tempered Nazarin who lives nobly following his own interpretation of Christ, is universally misunderstood. The poor glorify him as a new prophet; the powerful fear and loath his unorthodoxy and vigilance. In this world, being good is hard.

Title: Inglourious Basterds
Review: I postponed watching this for years, fearing I would dislike cheap action and annoyingly exaggerated characters. Instead I found myself pleasantly surprised. This is clearly a Tarantino film in spirit, and the idea of altering history in a way where the Nazis are depicted as ridiculously evil idiots, who are butchered to death this way is very clever and entertaining. I won't forget Hitler's disfigured corpse soon.

Title: Nosferatu, eine Symphonie des Grauens
Review: I have great respect for Murnau and have really enjoyed "Sunrise" and "City Girl" before this one. "Nosferatu" certainly is a well-crafted film too, but I think the silent genre does not combine well with the horror for me. Although the usual tension and fear that comes with horror films weren't absent here, I felt they were far less intense. I respect and enjoyed this, but its dated resources limited the experience.

Title: Waltz with Bashir
Review: Wonderful biography and history lesson reminding us that the cruel side of humanity is no thing of the distant past. The animations are nice and fresh, and the Max Richter soundtrack incredible. The ending of this film is one I won't soon forget: what an amazing release of emotional tension. Great film, although "The Congress" remains my favorite by Folman.

Title: Once Upon a Time... in Hollywood
Review: The adventure of life in which so much happens without immediate purpose, but in an incredible style that I could watch forever. Superb acting, lots of tongue-in-cheek and meta-level ideas, fitting music and beautiful long shots: wow! The most mature Tarantino I've seen, with a very enjoyable scene (out of the blue) of extreme violence concentrated in a fraction of the film. Everything was just right, incredible.

Title: A.I. Artificial Intelligence
Review: I'm usually put off by Spielberg's tendency towards sentimentality, but this lovely adventure truly moved me. Ethically this film is interesting in many ways: the little understood sentience of (some classes of) androids -which parallells the present-day situation of non-human animals- and the horrible state the environment is in. I would have preferred this film less mainstream, but it's really good nonetheless.

Title: Barefoot Gen
Review: Not sure whether to call it a children's movie or an adult traumatic drama, which demonstrates what an interesting mix this is. It's a very passionate memorial to the horrific bombings during WWII, and it provoked many emotions in me. The style is alternately delightful and dark, the message admirably optimistic: whatever happens, life goes on, and it's never worth giving up. Great film.

Title: Midsommar
Review: How does one ridicule a culture borrowing constituents from several traditions, religions and ideologies, while simultaneously praise its sense of worth and community and defend its right to exist? Ari Aster does it his -unique- way, combining traumatic horror and humor in the form of both mockery and random insanity. The experience is, just like Hereditary was, an amazing trip which I highly recommend. I'm a fan.

Title: Rocko's Modern Life: Static Cling
Review: Meet the 21st century through the eyes of 90s icon Rocko; such a clever script. I'm a fan of the show and I really enjoyed this comeback episode. It felt true to the original vibe, even the animation style was kept intact. There was only a slight cringe in regards to it being a comeback episode, which deserves praise too. Finally I want to add that I found it really cool they chose to go with Rachel's story!

Title: Pan's Labyrinth
Review: Wow, at times this was so dark the evil thrill went straight through my bones. I'm not a big fan of fairy tale lore, but I really liked the rendition in this film. I like how the promised kingdom is not shown, and how that entire world is really quite vague. It may not be entirely my cup of tea still, but this is a good film.

Title: Sex, Lies, and Videotape
Review: Great script creatively managing to make everying revolve around Graham's videotapes, with a touching climax involving Graham himself. I like how the otherwise realistic acting comes across a bit goofy in the context of this 80s/90s style. Very interesting and entertaining watch.

Title: Triple Frontier
Review: This was a surprisingly fun movie to watch. I'm not at all one to enjoy explosions and fast-paced action, but that was actually fairly limited in this film. Also, it had much more substance than that. The dark comedy revolving around the extreme amount of money that pretty much gets everyone to behave ridiculously is really nice. Ultimately though it's still quite formulaic and plain, but I liked it.

Title: Roma
Review: I love how this film succeeds in making you feel like an observer, both of a piece of history as of an intense, hard life of a working class woman. The acting and photography are amazing and greatly aid in the immersive effect. Everything's just so subtle. I particularly thought the baby scene and beach scene were incredible. Wonderful film adhering to a more classic style. I'm surprised this is a Netflix production.

Title: Behind the Curve
Review: It's hard not to ridicule a conspiracy theory as extreme as this one, but it's important not to engage in such ridicule. What I think the documentary did a very good job at is to highlight the religious aspect of it. I actually felt some jealousy when I saw their community, and the purpose they felt. And I have to note: it's funny how unfalsifiability is an important protector of religion.

Title: The Ritual
Review: I did not have high expectations, but was quite surprised by the rather emotionally intense opening scene. The film continued to do a good job by keeping up a dark, mysterious atmosphere, where I truly found myself captivated by curiosity. The beautiful forests, the clean style of filming, and the skillful blend of reality and nightmares were all nice. Sadly though, it ultimately turned incredibly cliche.

Title: The Favourite
Review: This film is so beautiful. All of its exterior qualities cooperate seamlessly to achieve that sense of mastery only great films have. Particularly the audiovisual way of storytelling by using crossfades and minimalist baroque music I found lovely. The cynical portrayal of those times make it a great dark comedy. Remarkably, the film has a quite accessible storyline, which debouches into a subtle and great ending.

Title: Paths of Glory
Review: I love how this film is deeply -and in a typical Kubrick sense- comical in the most dark, subtle way, all the while serving the function of mocking the absurdity of the concept of war to begin with: it's fundamentally cynical. But there's plenty of more serious scenes as well, such as the singing German lady, the prison visits and the trial. This perfect mixture of serious and comical has left me in awe!

Title: What Dreams May Come
Review: If you prepare yourself for Hollywood mediocrity this is an enjoyable film. It has lots and lots of sentimental cliches and problems of other sorts, but it does have some quality to it. Especially the heavens and hells are pretty interesting, the visuals in particular.

Title: L'âge d'or
Review: Wonderfully experimental, and at times I had to laugh out loud at the beautiful humor in this film. Buñuel proofs again that he's an extremely progressive filmmaker. The acting is really good and funny as well. I'm not entirely sure about the beginning of the film I must say though, where I might have gotten the wrong impression regarding what kind of film this was going to be. All in all a very nice film.

Title: De paardenbloem
Review: This is the masterpiece film that makes you laugh about, mindfully enjoy the desire of and feel weirdly erotically about food. It's incredibly virtuoso in so many ways. Somehow a film can borrow from westerns, be feel-good and funny in silly ways and still only be about the simple quest of perfecting ramen. And to emphasize: mindfulness is a big part of the viewing experience, but in a playful, ambiguous sense.

Title: The Cure
Review: Charlie Chaplin portraying an alcoholic? There was just no way this wasn't going to be fun!

Title: Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors
Review: Very unique film, throwing all kinds of qualities in the mix, visually, stylistically and emotionally. The story is incredibly heartbreaking. Their exceptional love suddenly gone, and how Ivan never really regains spirit, was so well entrenched in the viewing experience. Anthropologically this film is a very interesting watch as well, although I wouldn't know to what extent it's accurately realistic. Loved it.

Title: Fantasia 2000
Directors: James Algar,Hendel Butoy,Francis Glebas,Eric Goldberg,Don Hahn,Pixote Hunt,Gaëtan Brizzi,Paul Brizzi
Review: Hearing "Rhapsody in Blue" since again brought so much happiness and tears, so that alone already elevated the experience. I also liked the animated video accompanying it. The Firebird final animation also stood out for me. Overall it was a really nice experience, but something about it didn't feel as exceptional as you'd hope it to be.

Title: Dagvlinder
Review: Catherine Deneuve acts her double-life perfectly. Séverine is such a complex character! Her  a seemingly fragile, silent personality allows for the interesting contrast with her sexual, "lost" side. The least extravagant Buñuel I've seen so far, which did require my expectations to switch modes, but a wonderful piece of cinema, no doubt.

Title: The Lost Weekend
Review: This feels like a very progressive film for its time to me, utilizing a film-noir style creatively to support a sophisticated blend of comedy and drama, as a result providing both laughter and sadness. The story is timeless and acted out well.

Title: Hereditary
Review: Expecting a genre cliche, I could hardly believe what hit me. Certainly, many cliches were there, yet crafted masterfully, and the way they constitute the complex and full style proves ASTER is a true virtuoso. I have seldomly seen such an intense film, traumatizing the watcher with vivid hysterics that hit you out of the blue. It's creative, mysteriously vague and layered with interesting metaphors. Great film.

Title: The Discreet Charm of the Bourgeoisie
Review: Boy did I have fun watching this. A wonderfully sharp and playful satire of the elitist lifestyle, pretty much completely ridiculing it. The surrealistic touch has been mixed in properly to enrichen the experience, without leaving a trace of the sense of style inconsistency. Most of all the humor is just top-notch! It's wonderfully cynical, dry and subtle. Fantastic film.

Title: Female Vampire
Review: Even though I think this film isn't as deep as it thinks it is, it has certainly convinced me it's more than a cheap cover-up for a porn film. I did at times get caught in the magical, erotic atmosphere, thanks to the soundtrack and minimal presence of dialogue. In the end though, I was often bored and can't deny Lina Romay's beauty was a major reason to keep watching.

Title: The White Ribbon
Review: Not many people can make you feel as emotionally disgusted as Haneke can. Nothing of the cheap kind of however. This is a deep film which touches cleverly on the psychology of punishment (of children) and religious customs. Astonishingly, everyone, despite their deeds, is so pitifully human. The beautiful black and white production fully immersed me in this wicked tale. One of Haneke's most stylistic films I'd say.

Title: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
Review: Wonderful film, both deep and entertaining. I particularly loved Leamas, whose cynical character is so well-portrayed and psychologically profound. His entire character just radiates nihilism, yet finds purpose in the eternal waiting, the game one plays as a spy. This film made me look into the psyche of a spy like no film did before. Highly recommended work of art.

Title: Ecstasy of Order: The Tetris Masters
Review: Really cool documentary which shows how nice gaming communities can be. Also, the passion and obtained skill have made me appreciate speedrunners more in general. Very nicely done.

Title: Het vreselijk ontwaken
Review: I watched this in complete astonishment and awe. It's incredible how quickly things turn increasingly bizarre. An exceptionally funny film too, with the reverential status of beer and the incessant drunken adventures. Yet despite all the madness, the film is a deep, genuine exploration of the thin line between nihilistic chaos and civil life. To quote Doc: "Affectability... progress... are vanities spawned by fear".

Title: No
Review: A nice way to learn about politics is through film, where sensory experience accompanies the gathering of information. This film did this job perfectly: it has succeeded in celebrating this great event in recent history, meanwhile entertaining you using the absurdity of it all. There's also a deeper message I get from this film: sometimes, the rhetorical approach beats the honest, factual one. Time for me to grow up.

Title: Still Walking
Review: Very clean, dramatic cinema which is driven almost completely by acting, enabled greatly by the social situation the characters find themselves in. The film provides a really vivid account of (part of) Japanese culture and social etiquette. This slightly dry content is enriched by a serene, ambient style, consisting of tranquil shots and soothing, acoustic guitar music. Nice film.

Title: Gertrud
Review: In many regards this is clearly a Dreyer film: the existential crisis of Gertrud for instance, and the theatrical, poetic acting in the film. However, it couldn't completely captivate me for some reason. In a way it felt like, for me, the relative modernity of the film conflicted with the theatrical style elements. I did really love the story and theme though, and Gertud's open-minded and interesting choices in life.

Title: The Andromeda Strain
Review: A unique film which succeeded in turning dry, realistic scientific research into an interesting 'solve the mystery' kind of adventure. The style is great too, with the obscure synthesizer soundtrack and simple, solid-colored decor. The characters are quite typical on the one hand, but the film manages to mix in the right kind of self-mocking humor to put that to its advantage. Sci-fi classic!

Title: De dag des oordeels
Review: Dreyer is on his way to become one of my favorite directors. Repeatedly he shows great skill in treating conflict regarding religion and human psychology, all set against neat historical depictions of earlier ways of life. The dry style puts focus on the complex psychology at play, as seen clearly in this film. How the religious mind can dwell is often beyond my comprehension, and Dreyer captures just that.

Title: The Night of the Hunter
Review: This is a wonderful film in so many ways. The photography is beautiful, the ethics deceivingly complex, and most importantly: the adventure is amazing. I'd expect this film to be able to appeal to young children too, mainly because of the acting and the romantic approach in which the tale is shown, which gives the film its strong warmth.

Title: Wild Tales
Review: Wonderful concept for a film, and actually very funny too. These shorts remind me of Roald Dahl's short stories, which are similarly witty and darkly comical. Highly recommended to anyone with a great sense of humor who wishes to see something fresh.

Title: Louise by the Shore
Review: What's real and what's fantasy? You stop caring as soon as you let yourself immerse in the world of Louise. Marvelous style, both the drawing and the music. It is especially mesmerizing if you're familiar with (and I'm sure many of us are) that occasional desire of wanting to be all alone. Great little film!

Title: Huivering
Review: Unusually superficial for Cronenburg, but really enjoyable. It manages somehow to remain interesting, even though it's quite predictable. The idea is pretty cool in a cult-sci-fi kind of way, and the ending is beautiful. Definitely enjoyed this!

Title: 45 Years
Review: I had to figure out for some time whether I disliked the acting, or the characters they played. It turned out to be the latter: how dreadful is this couple! I'm not talking about the horrible, but very interesting situation the film centers around, but their unbearable lack of openness and dishonest communication. Even their better moments feel feigned, plastic. It's a good film, although it annoyed me a bit.

Title: The Player
Review: Without explicitly breaking the fourth wall, Altman still plays extensively with the medium of film. The absurdly comical, goofy display of life feels cartoonlike, which is probably what lets him get away with breaking so many rules of film-making, such as not to let people talk simultaneously and having your plot lead somewhere. And how about the 'happy' ending: the jerk wins maximally? Point proven, Mr. Altman.

Title: Election
Review: The high-school genre is a guilty pleasure of mine, but the guilty part doesn't apply to this film, as it is by no means typical. It's a playful and fun exploration of the human proces of growing up, both of adults and youngsters. It's an interesting story ethically (morally?) as well. Entertaining at the surface, this film somehow manages to hit something deeper that I can't exactly lay my finger on. Good stuff.

Title: O Brother, Where Art Thou?
Review: When watching a Coen brothers film I often find myself in conflict: do I appreciate their style -which typically includes combining what appears to be a straight-forward story, dark or dry comedy and soft touches of the surreal- or don't I? With this film, this was no different: I loved the music and the intertwined surrealism, but much of the story, the characters and comedy just didn't fully deliver for me.

Title: Missing
Review: Another interesting film about political corruption by COSTA-GAVRAS, consisting of roughly the same ingredients as Z, making it to a great extent as interesting as that one. MISSING is somewhat more sentimental and less raw, but it does have a score by VANGELIS. Bottom line: if you like realistic, interesting stories of political corruption, Z is a masterpiece and if you liked that you're going to like this  as well.

Title: Decalogue II
Review: An interesting ethical dilemma to state the obvious, but even more incredible perhaps is the acting here. We see human interaction at its purest, as well as internal moral conflict and the burden of deep suffering in life. There's so much to feel and ponder on with this film, braught forth by a relatively little plot. I adored it.

Title: Koyaanisqatsi
Review: This must be one of the most awesome experiences I've had in quite a while. Such beautiful symbiosis between Glass's music and Fricke's photography; storytelling without a single word spoken or written! This is truly virtuoso cinema. When NASA decides to send out a follow-up to their Golden Record they shouldn't forgot to include this film as an experiential document of what planet Earth and humans are all about.

Title: Vegucated
Review: I like the emphasis on the experience of (trying) going vegan from start to 'finish'. Other information is also shared, but the documentary wisely disinguishes itself from others by focusing on the aforementioned. As can be expected it also contains horrifying images from the factory farming industry, but it is properly embedded in the film. Maybe there's some cringy stuff at times, but it's certainly worthwile.

Title: Decalogue I
Review: Is God fiction to make life bearable for those who cannot face the void of existence? Are those without God, not accepting his existence, doomed to confront life without the grace of his love? Do we have a soul, or is conscienceness simply a complicated machinery achievable even by computers? Deep questions are explored here, although I felt a little more subtlety with regards to presenting them would have been nice.

Title: Unforgivable Blackness: The Rise and Fall of Jack Johnson
Review: Not often do documentaries impress me like this one did: it's absolutely perfect. Jack Johnson's life is one of the most interesting ones I've ever seen, and how it ties in with the racial issues -which in itself is an interesting history lesson- in the early 1900s USA is simply breathtaking. One of the most unique, real heroic stories ever told, including suffering, humor and politics. What else could one want?

Title: The Past
Review: As is the case with A SEPARATION, Farhadi is an excellent script writer, who casts brilliant actors to carry the dramatic load perfectly. It's dry cinema that one probably loves or hates though. Good film.

Title: Interstellar
Review: What to say here. On the one hand I really dislike the sentimentality and some of the acting and pseudo-science. On the other hand this is a beautifully crafted modern epic adventure which relates interestingly to contemporary problems and expected human suffering because of them. The soundtrack is amazing, and the adventure never ceases to excite. To me, this is a masterpiece gone bad in a mainstream genre.

Title: There Will Be Blood
Review: At first it seems a veracious film about the history of oil drilling and how it seemed to make fortune seekers and villages prosper. Soon this utopia starts showing some more sinister side, and slowly the greed takes its toll on people, turning them into monsters. Very accessible and nicely filmed movie, recommended to many.

Title: Chinatown
Review: Superb combination of a captivating detective adventure and a piece of art in which political and financial powers are exposed for the viewer to witness. The style of this film is amazing as well. As the film progresses the story and atmosphere becomes increasingly bizarre, climaxing in a beautiful ending. Fantastic film.

Title: Battling Butler
Review: Nicely written story, fun to watch. Not equally exhilarating all the time, but definitely entertaining. The final scene is marvellous!

Title: Game Over, Man!
Review: Mostly cliche, but nonetheless entertaining in a "I'm chilling", ambient sort of way. Some stuff was prety creative, such as the Skintendo body suit and when Alexxx faked his death by auto-erotic asphyxiation and didn't plan on having to watch the two bad guys make out and have sex. It deserves two stars maybe, but it doesn't feel fair to my other two star films which are better.

Title: De geheimzinnige ruitenvrouw
Review: I feel this is one film I should like, but I simply didn't. The acting felt uncomfortable, the progression of the storyline not as captivating as I would've wanted it to feel. The political side of the film wasn't emphasized the way I expected and is accompanied by weird, cheap sentiment mostly in a pretty uncredible mother figure. I don't know. It wasn't all bad, but nothing really good either.

Title: Porco Rosso
Review: Such a surprise. I've heard so little of this film, and it turns out to be one of my favorites by MIYAZAKI. I got completely immersed in the beautiful watery world, flying free as a pig. I love the humor too, it is really cheeky! The only thing keeping me from rating this 5/5 is the mysterious curse that supposedly has turned Marco into a pig. It felt out of place, as if a darling couldn't be killed. Great film!

Title: Altered States
Review: Easily brushed off as unscientific mumbo jumbo, the intellectual explorations are pretty cool and offer quite the philosophical treat. There's plenty of other things to be doubtful about though, such as the extremity of reversion, first with the ape on the loose, and later at the end with that kind of pure energy shape. Meanwhile, the romance becomes cheesier, yet with some meaning somewhere too. Mixed feelings.

Title: Netherlands
Review: So well thought through is the psychology in this film, it's amazing. VINTERBERG sells a story that would seem impossible to call real to its full extent, and not only does he make you believe it, he convinces you of every detail in the complex chain of events leading up to it. The acting, the script, it's all truly brilliant. Then to top it all off the open ending is highly interesting, leaving you to think.

Title: Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri
Review: The idea of the billboards provide an easy in for sentimental 'revenge porn', which can be decently entertaining, and in fact most of the time it was. Every now and then though I couldn't help but think Mrs. Hayes was too tough and cool for me to take it seriously. However, I really admired the way her humane side shone through as wel. Very decent watch for sure.

Title: Lady Bird
Review: I like how this film is colorful, playful, but also has great drama acting. The relationship between Lady Bird and her mom is is very credible and psychologically and emotionally authentic. Everything did feel a little high-paced though, as if an entire series has been crammed into 90 minutes. Also, sometimes it felt 'too girly' for my taste, although at the same time that's part of what made the eccentric style.

Title: Nashville
Review: This is exactly what you want from ALTMAN: grandly hectical, satirical with the typical goofy touch, pointless in many ways, secretly political and above all incredibly cosy and loveable. This lengthy film entertains naturally, slowly, like a great piece of ambient music which captivates you without trying too hard. I consider this a masterpiece, where ALTMAN's style truly blossoms without compromise or weak spots.

Title: Annie Hall
Review: It could easily be mistaken for yet another ALLEN movie, but even though it could be said to be based on similar formulae as many of his other films, this one stands out because of the authentic energy of the actors, and the vibe between them. KEATON's vitality and wild yet sweet character are beautifully contrasted against ALLEN's typical neurotic type. Very loveable film!

Title: Norte, the End of History
Review: Such a beautiful film this is. Thanks to its length it can extensively cover all perspectives involved in the story, as well as pace everything slowly in order to allow both the drama to have more impact, and to enable the stunning visuals to flourish. Realistic drama without frills to elevate the experience superficially: its quality speaks on its own.

Title: Thirty Two Short Films About Glenn Gould
Review: Informative, reasonably enjoyable, but I didn't quite like the style. The format of presenting this in what I'd call pseudo-shorts -since they are clearly related, and not an actual collection of independent, interesting shorts- does not work very well. I'm happy to have learned about GOULD's love for animals, his interesting philosophical ideas and kind character though.

Title: M*A*S*H
Review: As I experienced with SHORT CUTS, here too ALTMAN has succeeded in providing the sensation of having watched an entire series with lovable, interesting characters, all the while focusing on them and their goofy actions simply because the film is otherwise so aimless. You have to be open minded to the format and to the humor too, but I enjoyed this college-like comedy in the Korean war.

Title: The Triplets of Belleville
Review: Somehow I didn't expect this film to be so absurd, which turned out to be a pleasant surprise! The animation is very funny, the musical scenes are very nice, the style feels delightfully French and the story on a whole is silly, but works well for the film. I liked it.

Title: 3 Women
Review: I'm not entirely sure what to think of this film. It's definitely an interesting, worthwile watch, a good film in many regards. I love ALTMAN's playful, creative and varied style, time and time again. I think I wasn't prepared for such psychological absurdity, which rather than surprise me in a positive way, rather struck me as uncredible and odd. Mixed feelings for me.

Title: McCabe & Mrs. Miller
Review: The tale of a typical western tough guy who is on an endeavour to build saloons and be rich, who finds himself becoming increasingly infatuated with an usually strong woman, one feminists would be proud of, although her profession would nowadays be frowned upon. By showing the fragile, emotional side of the hero I feel ALTMAN has done something unique with a western. The theme song by COHEN wonderfully supports this.

Title: Thank You for Smoking
Review: I like how this film both shows in great detail how dirty and greedy Nick Naylor has to be, while also showing that he is just a normal human being like most of us who pays for his living and cares about his kid. It's amazing how well Naylor masters rhetorical skill. At times he even had me slightly sympathetic towards the idea that maybe he isn't to be judged so easily after all, since it does indeed regard freedom.

Title: Brief van een onbekende vrouw
Review: It takes skill to prevent this from being cheesy, and I think Ophüls did this remarkably well. I was put to tears near the end, such a beautiful story of romance this is. The way their paths diverge and then cross again is very moving and even though some things seem rather incredulous (like Stefan failing to remembering the love of his life) they are elaborated so well you start admiring this oddity. Beautiful film!

Title: The Hospital
Review: Very nice, layered film which has that lovely 70s vibe. I was impressed by George C. Scott's acting, who seamlessly blended comedy and drama into one another. His depression is interesting, and the hospital-centric approach even more so. As the film progresses in its second half, I feel it loses some of its focus though. But all in all I certainly enjoyed it.

Title: Black Swan
Review: It's nice to see Aronofsky bring the darkness of some of his earlier films out again, which he utilizes here to immerse you in the subtly growing insanity of the wonderful Nina. As with THE WRESTLER, here too the final phase of the film is a great climax. The swan parallell might be obvious, but is really nice nevertheless. Finally, the film is a pleasure to the eye.

Title: The Piano Teacher
Review: Edgy to the point where you would start doubting the psychological credibility of it all if it weren't done as brilliantly as it is. I found myself troubled and confused, not sure who to judge anymore, all the while being fed new extremities. I'm impressed Haneke turned this into something deeply interesting, as the subject is easily taken advantage of for cheap entertainment. Also: Huppert was absolutely perfect.

Title: De eeuwigheid en een dag
Review: How two stories of an old, dying, and a young, mistreated existence coincidentally intertwine, resulting in a highly unusual, but very pure and credible friendship. The nostalgic daydreming of Alexandros make me feel like I'm watching a Fellini film, but there's plenty other stylistic elements utilitzed by Angelopoulos, skillfully crafting this into a superb film. I don't think I'll ever forget that busride scene.

Title: Cléo from 5 to 7
Review: An incredible film by the great Agnès Varda with a beautifully crafted balance between artful delight and sober, slow-paced, realistic storytelling; an accomplished hint of experimentalism while remaining realistic at the surface. It's an amazing minimalist adventure of life that makes you experience truly the deepest possible powers of cinema.

Title: Mens, durf te leven
Review: A heartwarming film (thanks especially to James Stewart's natural charisma) that has all the elements for a great story and has them put together neatly: it's a very mature production that is a breeze to watch. However, something about its extremely Christian American, moralistic vibe (as with many more post-code 30s and 40s films) limits the fullness and authenticity of the experience for me.

Title: Z
Review: A masterpiece treating in vivid detail the inner workings of political corruption, covering several, if not all, layers involved in the process. It has the pleasant quality of providing intellectual depth and informative value, while keeping things down to earth and captivating. Every minute of this film is enthralling, and its content timeless and tragically human.

Title: In de macht van het monster
Review: Not usually a fan of the genre, this film certainly was certainly entertaining. The old dark house set in the stormy, rainy weather provides a nice setting, the characters are charming (as soon as you allow yourself to get used to them) and once the end nears I feel like the film is actually maturing ahead of its time.

Title: The Wind in the Willows
Review: Watching this as an adult, I found the animation wonderful and the style in its entirety heart-warming. What did bother me is the random, chaotic storyline, which almost feels as if they crammed a series-length of material into 80 minutes. This might be because I've watched it as an adult, hopefully children -the target audience- experience this differently. All in all it's very cosy and recommended for children.

Title: Pervert Park
Review: Does a good job providing an opportunity to show the victim side to being an sex offender. It reminds us that no human wants to commit horrible acts out of sheer wilfullness, but virtually always they've suffered a traumatic history or are mentally ill. Ultimately, they deserve to be considered human beings, receiving grace, all the while of course having to face the consequences of their actions.

Title: Het geheim van de katmensen
Review: At first it seemed too fantastical to me, but as the story progresses, it becomes darker and more mysterious and consequently -to me at least- more interesting. The mystery is supported well by the dark setting. I cannot help but dislike the fantastical bit though, even though it's the very unique and core thing about this film. A matter of taste of course.

Title: The Bat Whispers
Review: On the one hand I was very impressed by some of the camerawork and use of lighting and shadow, technique which seems progressive for the time. Sadly however, the film didn't interest me in any other way. I might not be a big fan of this genre maybe, but to me much of the film felt (too) silly.

Title: 5 Centimeters Per Second
Review: I love how this three-episode story does not ultimately give the viewer the most pleasing outcome, but the most painful and realistic one. It's a theme dear to my heart which is treated very well here. And such a mesmerizing setting! The beautiful animation enables this in a way that real life never could have you experience.

Title: Paterson
Review: Wonderful ambient film to watch when you long for tranquility. The soft fades from bus to scenery bring the mind to ease, supported by the slightly cheesy, but calming poetry written on the shots. The repetitive day-to-day plot supports the film's concept nicely, making it allround nice to watch.

Title: Anatahan
Review: Very convincing tragedy showing us how civilized men increasingly revert to cavemen, given they've had to endure sufficiently long the scarcity of primary resources such as food, love from familiy and friends, but most of all: sexual intimacy. It's remarkably well done how these people are still clearly modern and cultured, but in them primal forces are addressed under the pressing circumstances. Wonderful.

Title: The Phantom Carriage
Review: Remarkably moving film which tells the classic tragic tale of a man who abandons the virtuous life for a life of drinking and gambling. How extremely dark and bitter David Holm becomes struck me deeply, this causing Sister Edit's faith and deeds to become even more inspiring and beautiful. I watched this with tears in my eyes and enjoyed it allround: great film.

Title: Wind River
Review: The beautiful snowy landscapes are pleasant to watch, supporting the tranquil yet oddly negative atmosphere. Sadly, much of the film aims for slightly cheap revenge-orgasms and sentiment, with your typical loving father action hero. Still though, the film does possess qualities transcending that cliche as well. Overall it was a fun watch, but nothing particularly special.

Title: Come and See
Review: A masterpiece of cinema which captures the bizarre spirit of war perfectly by mixing in subtle absurdity with brutal realism, all the while maintaining a balance between art and adventure. Disturbing and traumatizing, and aesthetically superior, presenting beautiful raw photography with minimal music that seems somehow to cross the fourth wall. This is an exceptional piece of work.

Title: Peggy Sue Got Married
Review: What I liked about this film, other than the messed up voice Nicolas Cage puts on, is the warmth brought forth by the thought experiment it runs. However, much of it feels quite generic and I can't say it is a very special film as a whole.

Title: Uncertain
Review: You get the feeling they beat Werner Herzog to making this documentary, although stylistically it's certainly more tranquil and visual than most of his work. I really enjoyed the trip through the beautiful swampy landscape, as well as the bizarre stories of these people from Uncertain. Very interesting documentary, an easy and satisfying watch.

Title: Finding Dory
Review: The animation is great: no surprise there. I was very pleased, however, to find myself laughing quite a lot at the family-friendly jokes. Moreover, the film has a dark, emotional side that works really well. This is high quality Disney like I haven't seen in quite some time.

Title: Superbad
Review: Being a sucker for these high school comedies, a good time was pretty much guaranteed. It's a very nice adventure, written very well, which entertained me to the very end. Some of the humor was good, some of it was cheap, but overall I had a very good time. This is definitely a good one within the genre.

Title: It Comes at Night
Review: I love how this film takes a mysterious and psychological perspective, rather than being a usual apocalyptic action-adventure. It's low-paced and its nice, mature production naturally brings about a dark, truly creepy atmosphere. The paranoia, the survival-minded cruelty plaguing otherwise good people, Travis's growing up and mysterious development: it's done very nicely. And that daunting red door...

Title: The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water
Review: "Oh no, what happened to Saturn... and to Jupiteaaa". That line by the hilarious Bubbles completely cracked me up. There certainly is some other genuinely funny stuff, but overall it doesn't honor the Spongebob spirit very well and is clearly a commercial compromise.

Title: One Week
Review: Another very creative film by Buster Keaton, utilizing extraordinary means for the time it was produced. And it begs to wonder: how much was IKEA influenced by this? ;)

Title: Performance
Review: Probably just not my cup of tea. It felt like a hippie free-for-all orgie with absolutely nothing to hold on to. Every now and then I could appreciate some of the aesthetics and humor, but it just completely lacked anything to keep me interested most of the time.

Title: Fat, Sick & Nearly Dead
Review: Joe Cross's interesting green juice journey to weight loss was a fun watch. It was a breeze to see how he fearlessly talked to people about his adventure, inspiring people on the way. It's a shame he juices rather than blends (you want those fibers!) and doesn't understand what macro- and micronutrients are, but hey, he understands plenty to get the job done. I would've liked to have seen him gone vegan though ;).

Title: Computer Chess
Review: I was immediately taken by the subtly comical, geeky, quirky and minimalist style. The simultaneous presence of the therapy group invites for philosphical inquiry: emotional passion vs. intellectual curiosity, but there's more to it that I cannot grasp yet. Furthermore, I wasn't particularly impressed with how Peter started losing his sanity regarding chess 'going real life'. It was a nice and authentic film though.

Title: Root of All Evil?
Review: I respect Dawkins greatly as a scientist, educator and openhearted atheist advocate. This documentary however quite dramatically exaggerates the problem (at times comically), and it's a shame he acts so unpleasantly towards religious people, rather than engaging in proper debate in which case he could've deployed more creative arguments instead of passive agressive insults and might have actually inspired someone.

Title: The Earrings of Madame De...
Review: I wasn't immediately taken by the style of this film, because some elements of it reeked of the early 50s. However, as the movie advanced I was very impressed with Ophüls's creative ability to make the earrings the movie's star. And then there is the magnificent ending, which is simply amazing and washes away any sour taste one could've gotten during the first half of the film. Certainly very nice!

Title: Les cousins
Review: Such a tragic phenomenon in life: work hard and ... lose to the romantic aristocrat. Furthermore the path to love, for some, is paved with carnal desires. A classic tale told beautifully, with all-round great directing and production. This is one of my favorite French New Wave films.

Title: No Cow on the Ice
Review: A truly personal, authentic narration of a Spanish immigrant in Sweden. It's honest, educational and inspiring, its style an interesting blend of rough documentary-style video footage and a more aesthetic, ambient style revolving around still photography and meditative, natural sounds. A marvelous fusion of an inspiring personal story and a very aesthetic display of beautiful Sweden.

Title: How to Reach God Through Proper Exercising
Review: I don't mean to hate, but I simply didn't understand anything about this short. I sense a layer of symbolism that I can't grasp, and some stylistic elements feel pretentiously random. I don't like it.

Title: Royal Space Force: The Wings of Honnêamise
Review: What appears to be a story of the existential struggle of a youngster who discovers meaning thanks to love at first, turns to an unexpected, dark, more serious tone when it adds the political perspective of power, greed and war to the mix. But ultimately, the film transcends this story of the finite altogether, making you remember that you, friend or foe, are a human being in the grand cosmos. Marvelous film.

Title: Play It Again, Sam
Review: Very authentic, cool cult movie with an increasingly high likeability over time. Some of the reckless slapstick-like humor invoked feelings of vicarious shame at first, but they grow on you, mainly because they fit in so well with the furthermore experimental, fourth-wall breaking absurdity. The Casablanca parallel is nicely done, and I loved Allan's explicitly depicted fantasies at the end. Great film.

Title: Once Upon a Time in Anatolia
Review: From the immediate start it's clear this film's a visual beauty. Its tranquil style is really pleasant to watch, its pace meditative and its humor authentic and seriously good. I did feel annoyingly encouraged to focus too much on the plot, which made me lose sight (for a while) of the actual layer of importance: the existential one. The plot is arbitrary, this film is about people, about life. Very good film.

Title: Lo and Behold, Reveries of the Connected World
Review: As always I find Herzog's style pleasing. His genuine curiosity, thorough covering of the subject and ability to illuminate some unexpected perspective you hadn't thought of before as an actual problem -like the people suffering from wireless radiation- exemplify why. Overall it did feel a little incoherent though, possibly because it tries to cover too much material from diverse fields. A nice documentary.

Title: Star Wars: The Force Awakens
Review: On the one hand I'd say this might be the modern episode that is most true to the original trilogy; at times I felt like watching a remake of A NEW HOPE. On the other hand it's thoroughly drenched in Hollywood's mainstream soup, especially the dark-side seems raped. I like the addition of an existentially confused storm trooper, but I'm not too sure about grandpa Han Solo's part. Fun to watch, but not much more.

Title: Summer Wars
Review: A playful exploration of the dangers of letting our digital lives becoming increasingly dominant, especially allowing the system to arrange many of our society's needs. A bit too jolly for my taste, with too perfect coincidences, but certainly beautiful and moreover: relevant and inspirational. We should heed the film's message and try to come together as a species to resolve our global issues. Nice film.

Title: The Place Promised in Our Early Days
Review: The mystery of the tower serves a wonderfully romantic tale of sci-fi. The soundtrack accompanies the beautiful animations well, setting a timid, dreamy mood. The science is vague, almost fantasy-like, which fits the atmosphere but is often confusing. The social dimension of the film can also be hard to fully understand, but it's certainly not bad. Something tells me this film had more potential, but it was fun.

Title: The Congress
Review: Constantly developing in unexpected, vague, yet logical ways, this film maintains a perfect balance, turbulently displaying creative and interesting ideas while remaining coherent and captivating. Genuinely philosophical on several levels, superseding just the rational and even utilizing the medium of film itself ingeniously. It even succeeded emotionally, peaking at the inventive ending which put tears to my eyes.

Title: Possession
Review: A powerful experience film full of intense, expressive acting, absurd humor in the form of ridiculously (often bloody) fights, demonstrating a funny, highly cynical point of view on love. It is this cynicism and dark humor I love about the film, but I didn't care for the many symbols and some of the random, expressionistic scenes it seemed to contain. Generally a neat, authentic style, but not entirely my cup of tea.

Title: 12 Monkeys
Review: Unexpectedly more mystery than sci-fi, focusing mostly on the mystery behind the virus outbreak rather than on its effects and character. This is neatly supported by the freaky style: a drooling B. Willis, steam-punky setting, weird zooms and oblique shots, this way creating a suppressive, bizarre atmosphere much like BRAZIL does. A very impressive script, of which I regard the climax surprisingly pleasing.

Title: The Green Ray
Review: A film about feeling disconnected even though being amidst people with good intentions who are incapable of truly listening or understanding, about desparate attempts to rediscover oneself through holidays during which one meets people but feels not less alone. A realistic exploration of the introverted, but lost mind, presented in an aesthetically pleasing film that makes you feel you're on vacation. A masterpiece.

Title: Going Clear: Scientology and the Prison of Belief
Review: South Park actually didn't exaggerate: this 'religion' is completely ridiculous. This documentary has taught me it's far worse than that though. Ex-members, most of them highly ranked or senior, tell their stories of extreme mental and physical abuse, indoctrination and money scamming: it's appalling. Moreover, their perspectives really gave me a unique peak in the mind of a believer. Highly recommended.

Title: The House of Small Cubes
Review: Even though it feels like yet another creative short film on the one hand, it can't be denied it fulfills its destiny well. Wonderfully nostalgic, with a befitting style constituting of cute drawing and heartwarming music. It's adorably creative in the way it carries its emotional theme. Worth your while!

Title: Angst essen Seele auf
Review: A tale of everyday ethics, in which kind-hearted Emmi proves that no setback is grave enough for her to give up her kindness, symbolizing the power of forgiveness and trust. I like the mild, pleasingly theatrical style, which allows for the dry humor and slight magnification of emotions, giving it a warm, romantic touch. At the same time though, it is clean and realistic cinema: a beautiful combination, done neatly!

Title: Socrates
Review: An entertaining and leisurely educational film about our favorite ancient Athenian philosopher Socrates, which features some well-known epigrams, but sadly doesn't show Socrates' comical side at all, which in my opinion is quite a missed opportunity and flaw. Furthermore, it's pretty dry and long-winded, although the trial scene is good. Not a perfect biography maybe, but an interesting historical film nonetheless.

Title: Before the Flood
Review: Interesting conversations with experts in various disciplines and from many different places; footage of several locations around the globe where the devastating effects of global warming can already clearly be seen, often striking the poorest of people; a critical view on the responsibility of western civilization, especially the USA and even its politicians. Also, it's an accessible production for a large audience.

Title: The Passion of Joan of Arc
Review: I recognize the incredible achievement of Dreyer in this early age of film, but the necessity of an exaggeratedly visual display of emotions limits its touching effect. Unlike some FW Murnau films from the same period which are accompanied by music, this feature was entirely silent, making it harder to stay focused. The camera was used very impressively, aesthetically exposing the clear power and status differences.

Title: The Jungle Book
Review: As a child this was one of my favorite movies, so this remake had quite a lot to live up to, especially since I strongly favor drawn animation over CGI. It may be partly due to these bad expectations that the film turned out to be quite fun! The atmosphere is nice, the story kept well intact, and most important of all the characters stayed true to the classics. Not as great as the original maybe, but certainly fun.

Title: My Girlfriend's Boyfriend
Review: A playful film in which we are taught how comically wrong our intuitions can be. As always, Rohmer knows how to balance realistic emotions and social interactions, and playful situations that are just unlikely enough to happen in real life to serve the comical purpose. On another note: how incredibly beautiful are those suburbs of Paris? Beautiful film in each and every way.

Title: The Model Couple
Review: A clumsy, almost amateurish production, yet not without charm. Its style is without doubt one of a kind and even though I did not find it highly aesthetically pleasing, it is particular and fun. I'm equally unsure about the deeper layer of the film: the experiment feels a bit inefficient to me in terms of what it seems to try proving and it all feels a bit awry. All in all it was a fun watch, but not much more.

Title: Mad Ladders
Review: Stunning visuals and nice music. This is experimental in a way that beats pretence and is actually nice.

Title: Limitless
Review: The concept is interesting, although much of the science and some of the drug's effect don't make too much sense. I was surprised by the nice acting of Cooper and really enjoyed the interesting visual effects and editing in this film. During the second half I lost most of my interest, but I did like the ambiguous ending! It really invites to think through the possibility of his brain actually having changed. Decent!

Title: Taro the Dragon Boy
Review: As much as I enjoyed this now, boy would I love to have seen this as a child. This film's a great teacher in compassion, which at times even caused tears to appear in my eyes. Such authentic drawing, beautiful music and simply a charming style overall. I really enjoyed this beautiful film.

Title: I Heart Huckabees
Review: A mid 00s charming and fun indie films, but certainly not compromising on philosophical depth. I usually have a tough time with such crafted films that experiment with conventional realism, but this film pulled it off nicely. The philosophical topics in the film are explored well, roughly stated comparing the 'everything is connected' buddhist metaphysics to the 'nihilist' perspective, both of which have their role.

Title: The Wizard of Oz
Review: Being fairly familiar with its story due to references from animated sitcoms and a probable watch during my childhood, I was surprised how much fun of a watch this film was! Such a massive production for its time, in which everything has been carried out to the last detail. A neat score, a beautiful decor and suiting costumes to finish off the style. The lion is a blast, he honestly made me laug out loud sometimes!

Title: Earthlings
Review: This documentary is one big compilation of raw (undercover) video footage showing animals being gruesomely abused in all related industries. I believe that, without passing judgment on people, we should all take responsibility and watch this, to educate ourselves about how our consumption causes countless animals to suffer and die horrific deaths every day, and try to do the respectable thing, which is to go vegan.

Title: District 9
Review: An interesting thought experiment that utilizes the alien theme for socio-political critique, most notably difficulties concerning immigration.
