Although I appreciate this, I wasn't too impressed with the film. I disliked the actors and the characters they portrayed, did not care for the alien CGI -except for the awesome spaceship- and think the storyline is one of a cliche action film. Scores on authenticity though.

Title: Law Abiding Citizen
Review: A cliche Hollywood production, although one with a tolerable production formula. As far as entertainment is concerned, the first half of the film is pretty nice, and actually reminded me of that delicious satisfactory feeling of revenge in "Taken". However, about halfway through it spins out of control, losing all credibility and remnants of authenticity. Not worth your while.

Title: New Kids Nitro
Review: Being from Noord Brabant myself, I can verify this is authentic behavior if you go look in the right neighbourhoods. Certainly an entertaining watch, although I liked the series of video clip a lot better.

Title: Hardcore Henry
Review: I'm no big fan of action hero movies, but this film definitely does a great job looking like a video game. I mean wow, everything makes sense from that perspective: the mystery around Henry, his cyborg nature, the weirdly overpowered 'final' boss. The camera-angle and editing in this film are amazing as well, of a level you'd expect only from a high budget Hollywood film. Lots of respect, however still not my style.

Title: Birdboy: The Forgotten Children
Review: The bizarre story didn't really appeal to me, although it certainly did contribute to the fun I had watching this beautifully animated film. It's something else for sure, but just not my cup of tea.

Title: Inherent Vice
Review: I love how this film gradually evolves from a decent, normal atmosphere to a more and more sinister, complex, druggy one. The style is mature and very pleasing, including the acting, particularly by Waterston and Phoenix. I'm unable to say whether it's open for interpretation or in fact just so complicated I wasn't able to get a clear picture, but either way it is brilliantly put together.

Title: Enter the Void
Review: What an experience this was. Its authentic, extreme and visual style represents tripping better than any other film I've seen or can imagine. The script is great, living in perfect symbiosis with the style, through which the emotional storyline is told interestingly and fittingly. A beautiful experience film, that makes you feel rather than think, although certainly not without a message.

Title: De samoerai
Review: The typical Melville style of the crime genre, yet in an -even for his sake- above average ambient setting. This makes this film stand out in his ouvre in terms of authenticity, although I have to admit it did not appeal to me as much as some other of his films. Nonetheless, quality stuff.

Title: Fitzcarraldo
Review: What a beautiful piece of art. An entrepeneur planning on bringing opera, his passion, to the Amazon by building an opera house there, only to fail yet succeed. A marvelously romantic idea carried out to the most bizarre level of detail as Herzog is capable of doing. The pacing, the creative ideas, the bizzarre adventure: it's complete. Also, an unusually serious role than I'm used of by Kinski and he acts well!

Title: My Dinner with André
Review: Amazing film. The dialogue is exceptionally realistic and the discussion is simply perfect in both a philosophical and psychological sense. It affected me deeply on a personal level, since the theme discussed is one that has haunted me -and undoubtedly many people- for the last few years: am I really living? Beautiful treatise on the art of living.

Title: Coffee and Cigarettes
Review: To be honest, much of this was pretty boring and only some of the scenes were actually funny. The concept is quite nice, but some of the recurring references and ideas are quite dull. Not recommended, although I can't say it was a complete waste of my time.

Title: Bob le flambeur
Review: Took a long time for this film to catch my attention, and it never did for long. Bob didn't speak to me much as a protagonist, and gambling isn't entirely my cup of tea either. I appreciate the film though. It has a lovely soundtack and consistent, "free" style, which I can imagine was progressive for its time. Loved the lawn used for heist practice by the way. All in all this was no more than enjoyable to me though.

Title: Short Cuts
Review: This film understands life. Did you even think about the medfly disaster after an hour? There's always something like that, but everyday life issues take over, always. The humor and absurdity further confirm comprehension of the nature of life, and especially the role of love and its difficulties. It has a wonderful, jazzy style, with deliberate overacting at times and much camera movement. And that beautiful intro!

Title: The Time Masters
Review: Much of the characters and storyline seem inconsistent and odd, but as with Laloux's other films the depicted world is amazing, especially the drawing style and colors. Also, I believe this is more intended as a film for children than the previous ones, which possibly accounts for the former 'defects'. I particularly loved the planet Gamma 10. Definitely a fun watch, probably even more so for children.

Title: Dog Day Afternoon
Review: In a way this concept has been done many times, but never like this. There's a clear political tone in the crowd's admiration of Sonny, particularly his stance on "Attica". Unbelievable acting by particularly Al Pacino, and a lovely, subtle suspense throughout this clean, great production. It was a great watch recommended for just about anyone.

Title: Serpico
Review: Lovely clean cinema, with a beautiful story and a perfect performance by Al Pacino. It struck me as a romantic, one-dimensional predecessor of the series "The Wire" in film form in a way. Remarkable and unique.

Title: Boccaccio 70
Directors: Vittorio De Sica,Luchino Visconti,Federico Fellini,Mario Monicelli
Review: How I loved the priest that was cruelly beat by his instinctual, sexual arousal towards Anita Eckberg. All of the four acts were weirdly comical and carried on a style of their own. Credits in particular to Visconti's set: marvelous. It was certainly a fun watch, although not something essential.

Title: A Scanner Darkly
Review: While being immersed in a druggy reality that feels increasingly absurd and comical, you are presented with a minimally worked out, paranoid dystopia, leaving the viewer puzzled in a vibe of mystery. The visual style is like in "Waking Life", but less hysterical, suiting this film's atmosphere well, more specifically enabling neat rendering of the scramble suit. A new type of Linklater, yet still very much his style.

Title: Iverson
Review:
Practice? We talkin' 'bout practice man?
Seriously though, a fun documentary that honors this great player well.

Title: The Forbidden Room
Review: This certainly is one of the most bizarre films I've ever seen. A neat crucible of parody on silent film, druggy trips and randomness, which is very funny at some times -the Aswang bananas and Janus-crazed intellectual come to mind- yet dull at others. The INCEPTION-like layeredness becomes tiresome after a while and so does the incessant introduction of new characters. Still, it's certainly enjoyable and authentic.

Title: Army of Shadows
Review: This film sheds an interesting light on the French resistance, displayed in a great, typical Melville style. Slow pacing with zooms that fulfill a narrative purpose, aesthetic wide shots and intense emotional situations veracious enough to speak for themselves. Something about the whole is slightly sloppy and there are some moments that ring less truthworthy, but it's a good film for sure.

Title: Full Moon in Paris
Review: As always Rohmer knows how to surprise in terms of quality within the same formula time after time. Yet another romance that goes bad among all his films, but once again he succeeds in getting the job done. It's real, it's interesting and it's fun. You simply can't go wrong with Rohmer.

Title: Me and My Gal
Review: I'm not sure what to say. Sometimes I felt vicariously ashamed, especially with the sidekick detective that seems to suffer from echolalia. Other times I laughed out loud: there are some witty conversations in there, and the drunks -although it takes a while before you realize how cynical it all is- are great, especially in the fish-slapping scene. I was nicely amused by this!

Title: The French Connection
Review: Great film with a slow pace and extensive use of camera movement and zooming that really suites the mysterious feel it has throughout. Hackman plays a great indocile detective whose gut feeling fuses well with the overall atmosphere. Best of all I enjoyed the great car chase scene, which is a big compliment, since I usually cannot be bothered much with such suspense.

Title: The Nightmare Before Christmas
Review: This film feels as much authentic Burton as it can get. I am usually no big fan of the theatrical, musical style, but I have to admit it's done really well. The idea of making Halloween and Christmas separate worlds that comically mix up is very fresh and fun. Neatly done, authentic and pure, just not my style though.

Title: Before Sunset
Review: Possessing pretty much the same qualities and flaws (if any) as its predecessor, this film is an excellent continuation. It once again makes you experience the most perfect possible romantic happenstance, and what makes it so hard to bear is its realistic value due to the amazing dialogue and emotional interaction. I'm really looking forward to seeing the last film in the trilogy, Linklater is a genius.

Title: I Killed My Mother
Review: A funny mixture of styles, notably borrowing slow, music-driven scenes from IN THE MOOD FOR LOVE. Sometimes it feels as if Dolan tries to hard, but this very inexperience adds to the authentic feel of the film. Hubert struck me as annoying at times, but perhaps I should consider that a quality of the film since this rebelling behaviour is faithful to reality. All in all, this is good arthouse cinema.

Title: Ben-Hur
Review: Marvelously epic and adventurous, making it a pleasure to watch, but far too sentimental and cheesy to consider it truly great. The ending is the absolute worst possible. But still, it's an entertaining heroic adventure.

Title: Two Days, One Night
Review: Such an unusually accessible, pleasing tension for a Dardenne film. While staying true to their realistic style, in some sense this film feels more fresh and less depressing than others. In some sense it seems to have an additional dimension of creativity involved that former films lacked. The moral dilemma is complex and interesting, peaking when Sandra is confronted with it herself at the end. Beautiful.

Title: Bloedlink
Review: The film is decorated and shot nicely, making it a pleasant watch. The synth-heavy proggy soundtrack feels out of place, the music is good on itself though. Sadly, I can't say the story interested me much to be honest, which is a big critique on this particular film that seems to rely on plot and suspense. It was an okay film with some qualities, but in my opinion that's all.

Title: Gang Related
Review: Yes, much about this film is bad and cliche, but it's funny as hell. Their crafty interrogation techniques to scam someone from the streets, the reflective discussions in which the clandestine Belushi comes up with hilarious reasonings to keep his friend aboard. I really enjoyed this film, even though it gradually turns more and more cliche along the way.

Title: L'Avventura
Review: When it gradually dawns on you that Anna's gone, there remains this subtle tension of expectation for her return throughout the film. Not able to grasp the loss, Sandro and Claudia try to resume their normal lives, but it's clear they can't. Apart from some spontaneous small moments of joy—the lovely church bells scene comes to mind—they are mourning, as becomes clear to hem in the beautiful final scene. Masterpiece.

Title: The Great Beauty
Review: Sure it borrows the theme of partying socialites suffering from an existential crisis and a Rome-centric viewpoint from LA DOLCE VITA, but it has plenty of authenticity as well. It's less distant, more personal, and as I recall the style of filming differs greatly. I liked the moving camera in this film, and even though I wasn't always impressed with the humor and absurdities, it certainly was refreshing to see.

Title: Rust and Bone
Review: Such realism and coherence in a film that is so eclectic at the same time, alternating between -among other facets- dry, genuine dramatic events and slow, aesthetic visuals and dreamy sequences of reminiscence. Then there's the ambiguous love story of an agressive asshole who's also an amazingly considerate human being and a woman who struggles with the loss of her legs. And the kid on the ice scene? Wow. Loved it!

Title: Citizenfour
Review: Snowden's revelations concerning citizen privacy may start to become common knowledge by now, but actually seeing the process of his emergence documentend in this film adds an entire new dimension to the story. His just personality, the strategy of not releasing all information at once but passing it on gradually through journalists, the media response and the effect on his personal life... It's just really amazing.

Title: Deep Web: The Untold Story of Bitcoin and Silk Road
Review: An informative documentary that sheds a different light on the otherwise so darkly portrayed Silk Road and its founder Ross Ulbricht, suggesting good intentions on his behalf to push back drug related crime and utilize the potential of an (extremely) free market. Although I can't be sure who tells the story right, it certainly is a sad one, likely unfair. Can we trust our government and legal system? I doubt it.

Title: Cowspiracy: The Sustainability Secret
Review: Very versatile, concise and informative documentary which tactically prioritizes the environment over animal treatment —which certainly gets attention too—, thereby emphasizing the absolutely important perspective to anyone. Many of the arguments and calculations are easy to follow, which contributes to the credibility and comprehensibility of this film. This film actually might have persuaded me to go vegan.

Great style with an incredible camera that creates a videogame-like experience. The concept of robot dolls carrying parts of a soul is neat. Two of them becoming romantically involved however is terribly cliche and wrong. Also, once souls are freed from The Machine they fly off to the sky? Please. Still, The Machine is amazing, especially in the 'Somewhere over the rainbow' scene which is exceptionally beautiful.

Title: Coraline
Review: An adorable film that teaches children the grass is always greener on the other side, and it does this in a very creative and appealing way. The stop-motion style is beautiful and there are some really interesting, absurd, almost avant-garde scenes, like the circus performances and the garden. Loved the button-for-eyes detail and its subtle hint of darkness. Good film!

Title: Terms and Conditions May Apply
Review: A wake-up call for those —myself included— who think they've got nothing to hide. This documentary explains how profiling by big data companies is used by governmental agencies and what consequences this has both potentially and currently. The stories about individuals who were flagged as suspicious really made an impression on me. Our freedom of speech is at stake, so best get informed and take action.

Title: Chappie
Review: From a cult perspective this film is quite okay. This accounts for the typical 'tough guy turns lovable' and 'evil good guy' cliches, and also for some of the ridiculous humor, which then makes sense at times. Chappie is a very nice looking robot and the idea of transferring consciousness is an interesting sci-fi classic. It was a fun watch. Fun detail by the way: all of the computers seem to be running on Linux.

Title: Inside Llewyn Davis
Review: I loved the color palette and the dull, depressed feel throughout the film. The mysterious car trip and dark humor involving John Goodman was the highlight for me. In general I felt like lots of symbolic meaning went straight over my head. After reading more about the film some pieces of the puzzle started to fit though. Not a very big fan of much symbolism, but this film kept it within bounds. Overall I liked it.

Title: Wild Strawberries
Review: We get to live the life of the old prof. Borg, who suffers from an existential crisis when he's awarded for his achievements. He's troubled with nostalgic, dreams of his younger years, which has a really immersive effect. Furthermore his benignity is challenged by his daughter-in-law —who happens to travel along in this roadtrip-like journey— leading to an interesting discovery of who he really is. Beautiful film.

Title: The Lobster
Review: Our conception of love is ridiculed and honored at the same time in this absurdistic exploration. The cynicism is layered and funny, and the surrealistic touch together with the great photography and soundtrack constitutes a very nice atmosphere. Towards the end it becomes a bit uninspired though, and something about the whole feels a bit unpolished, suggesting Lanthimos's style might still be maturing. Very nice.

Title: Pauline at the Beach
Review: The characters and social-emotional interactions between them are Rohmer-worthy, yet this film pulls off to be a lot less dry than most of his films, making it accessible to many people who get bored by Rohmer's otherwise plain, slow, plot-light style. The topic of what makes people attract each other romantically is unusually exposed and universally interesting, and the plot develops well. One of Rohmer's best.

Title: A Good Marriage
Review: What a performance by Béatrice Romand! Sabine is that real-life character that both annoys and fascinates you. She acts infantile and playful in a ridiculous fashion, but somehow it suits her and actually makes her genuinely attractive. Rohmer's talent to create enthralling films with barely any significant plot keeps on amazing me.

Title: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya
Review: With a folklore feel truly unseen before this film enchants you with its authentic and minimal style. Its brushy art-style, folky music and dominant nostalgic desire for a simple life in accordance with nature embracing both the good and the bad: all of this constitutes a harmonious, consistent style. It seems less accessible than most Ghibli films, so it might be suited for melancholic anime lovers only.

Title: Green Street Hooligans
Review: An Ivy League student that turns to hooliganism this passionately? Uncredible. Furthermore the film tends to glorify hooligans in a way, the 'we are brothers and have each others back' angle. Unnecessary since it's childish and ridiculous. Cliche characters and over-the-top produced violence. There's basically nothing in here.

Title: Dheepan
Review: Unlike many other arthouse films, this film is more than just a story and play on sentiment. There is emotional complexity that makes you hate, then understand, feel sorry, but at any rate makes you feel. But the story certainly develops interestingly too, up to the point where Dheepan loses it and goes berserk. The atmosphere and cinematography here is incredible: you can live his panic right through the screen.

Title: Charles Mingus: Triumph of the Underdog
Review: The documentary is a bit dry, but that does also account for the genuine feel to it. It gives an interesting peak into the life of this wonderful artist, including interview material and cuts from concerts. Recommended for those interested in Mingus, however it might not be suited for initiating newcomers to his music.

Title: De vreemdeling zonder naam
Review: Starring Clint as a cynical, egotistical asshole, this movie is creatively cruel with the right amount of absurdity to make it funny. I like that the entire city is treated like shit, except for the town midget and Indians. I like how he eventually turns out to be no bigger asshole than the town's inhabitants. My only dislike was of the spiritual overtone with the beaten-to-death sheriff which is just plain stupid.

Title: Songs from the Second Floor
Review: Absurdly humorous and still full of subliminal, symbolic critiques, particularly of the socio-economic status quo. Presented in an emphatically theatrical style with gorgeous shots, this film certainly is oddly authentic: nothing really compares to it. Comic exaggeration of little bizarre incidents, weirdly repetitive poetic utterings, and silences and settings that cause a Kafka-like alienation. Wonderful film.

Title: Leviathan
Review: While initially suggesting a pretty straightforward plot, it gradually moves away from this focal point to exhibit what I consider the central concept of the film, the concept of power, in several forms, including masculinity, beauty, politics and religion. The dark production is beautiful and the acting is realistic and appealing, even though at times the stereotypical drinking and smoking is a bit much. Good film!

Title: Melancholia
Review: The first part felt like an okay but dime a dozen Dogma 95 film. The second part is simply brilliant. Overwhelming both visually and auditively on account of the growing circle and omnipresent roaring. In a unique way people are shown trying to cope with this unexpected immense event. I disliked some of the cheap shocking and bizarre Kirsten Dunst scenes though, nor did I feel much for the mystical layer. Good film!

Title: Henry: Portrait of a Serial Killer
Review: This is one of those films that has an authentic atmosphere enforced on it due to a low budget. Some of the shooting is nicely done, and I quite enjoyed the soundtrack at times too. It's very disturbing, but somehow not such that you're tempted to turn it off all the time. Henry is an appealing -but insane!- protagonist, Otis is the disgusting hanger-on. If you're in the mood for something sick, this is quite nice.

Title: The Aviator's Wife
Review: Again and again Rohmer sheds light on the ambiguous nature of romantic relationships, each time with renewed creativity. The arguments and emotional dynamic between François and Anne is recognizable to many, and in a subtle way Rohmer makes you chuckle at the ridiculousness of it all. Then there's Lucie and her adventurous spontaneity, which really adds an extra dimension to this film. It's deep but witty. Very nice!

Title: Synecdoche, New York
Review: Even though the trick feels old, it's executed nicely. As usual P.S. Hoffman plays a very credible, neurotic loser, who greatly supports the psychotic, insane atmosphere of the film. I really enjoyed the bizarre humor and the eerie feeling throughout the film. Afterwards I caught myself trying to figure the film out rather than to dispose of it as cheap trickery. Once again this emphasizes the film's quality.

Title: Sharknado
Review: Just as bad as part two which I watched first -I'm sure that didn't matter- but this one seems to try a little harder as if it takes itself even only slightly seriously. That hurt.

Title: Sharknado 2: The Second One
Review: I really wanted to give it two stars because it certainly did enjoy me, but it simply wouldn't be fair towards the actual two star rated films. Horrible in all possible ways, but certainly ridiculous enough for some superficial laughs.

Title: Forbidden Planet
Review: Visit your local library and pick up some physics books from which to quote randomly. Then, ask your handy uncle Tom to help you build a robot. Realise you're living in the 50s and cast an unnecessary, innocent but sexy girl who serves perfectly for innuendo, unbounded by the laws of decency. This is probably how the charming but ridiculous Forbidden Planet came to be. Great laughs though, and charmingly handmade!

Title: Selma
Review: Even though I was mainly disappointed by the formulas guiding me to have specific emotions at certain times, particularly by the use of sentimental music, there were some moments that really moved me and made me profoundly realise the potential power of political activism. It's just a very inspirational story with great historical significance, which makes up for the relatively boring and bad cinematic value.

Title: Woyzeck
Review: In this great parody of life things like status and scientific overvaluation are ridiculed dryly. I laughed out loud at the fanfares playing awfully dissonant with the mooing of cattle right through it. Then there's the absurd character of Woyzeck, sometimes funny, sometimes compelling. In some way the film makes little sense, but it's so charming and appealing. Loved the end of the film, and what a charming town!

Title: De mummie
Review: Historically interesting early entertainment work, but not my kind at all. I disliked just about everything, except perhaps for the awakening of Inhotep. I've seen much more interesting films from this era, which weren't as poorly directed too.

Title: Rode woestijn
Review: As Giuliana meanders through the heavily industrial setting as well as through her life, feeling anxious, absentminded and disconnected, we experience this with her. No scene is completely deprived of this sense of alienation and growing insanity, not even the very humorous one on the bed. Perfect photography with eerie minimal electronic music to create just the right atmosphere. This is a masterpiece.

Title: Watchmen
Review: This film filled 215 minutes trying to combine philosophical depth with cheap sensationalism and action. I mean, that's like trying to unite left and right wing politics. Infantile dress-ups, weird character developments and assessments and clichéd Hollywood formulas all over. If only everything wasn't done so ridiculously awful, I might have respected the darkness and ethical ambiguity. So all in all, horrible.

Title: Night Moves
Review: What I loved is those few seemingly meaningless shots of random people doing everyday stuff. These make you experience so vividly the distance between Josh and his ideals and the average Joe, and also understand him better. His realistically paranoid, odd behavior contributes to this, as does the slow pace, gloomy atmosphere and great photography. Its grand message is told not in words, but by inducing an experience.

Title: Whiplash
Review: What starts out as a rather predictable drama about a ruthless teacher wracking a timid pupil turns out to be a peek in the minds of those obessively persuing greatness. Andrew's puzzling emotional development eventually becomes clear: he and Fletcher are alike, desiring be great at any cost. A true ode to genuine jazz music, ending with an incredible drum performance. I bet the girl wished she went to the concert!

Title: Goodbye to Language
Review: Usually I like his way of experimenting, but the way 3D is raped here feels unnecessary and annoying. Granted though, it being Godard, he kind of had to do it. Much of it feels like a generic instance of his style, with the hit and miss poetry and absurd symbolic events. However, I liked the trippy colorings, loved the dog and also his purpose in the main philosophical point of the film, which really appealed to me.

Title: Liefde en-gros
Review: A tale of platonic love and art versus carnal desire and lust, revolving around Gilda, the mother of the arts, the heart of the love triangle. Although the plot seems rather superficial, it is very well written, including witty dialogues and clever symbolism. I am usually no fan of theatrical exaggerations, but here it's done so consistent and well that I was able to embrace it. A very charming and mature film.

Title: Birdman
Review: On the one hand it's yet another allegory for an existential crisis of a celebrity, on the other it certainly has a refreshing style. It's jazzy, goofy and theatrical, but it didn't always work for me. Sometimes it's simply too exaggerated or on the nose, especially Edward Norton annoyed me at times. Also, I think the film should've ended earlier. Still, a great performance by Keaton and a nice satirical movie.

Title: Breaking the Waves
Review: Wow. I have not been this emotionally wrecked by a movie in a long time. Such emotional complexity and depth involving feelings of guilt, faith and inferiority with a touch of sexual absurdity. Bess is an amazingly fascinating person, such marvellous acting by Emily Watson! She really moved me. Strongly preferring Von Trier's older films, I deem this his best.

Title: Clouds of Sils Maria
Review: During the first part the discussions about the play and acting struck me as a bit pretentious and tedious. Particularly the actress-persona parallell seemed cheap. As the film progresses though, the parallell becomes more profound and Maria's midlife crisis becomes credible and interesting. And such great chemistry between Binoche and Stewart! Ultimately though, I think the film lacks constancy of quality and style.

Title: Ida
Review: This film cleverly wraps an inquiry into an Apollonian (Ida) and Dionysian (Wanda) lifestyle in a moving, modest adventure of post-war family drama, and does so quite impartially. Furthermore, it has a clean cinematic style with the most beautiful photography I've seen in a long time. Good on all levels, with an ending that suits it well, this is a lovely film.

Title: Madeliefjes
Review: Two spoilt, flirtatious girls acting randomly at the expense of others, who don't understand love -their excessive meat-eating may symbolize carnal desire- and doubt their existence when not acknowledged by others. Full of criticizing allegories and symbolism, this piece of visually creative eyecandy leaves room for lots of interpretation. A bit too random and infantile for me at times, I certainly enjoyed this film.

Title: Only Lovers Left Alive
Review: An interesting, fresh exploration of the struggle of vampires in the 21st century, coping with existential and moral problems as well as with survival in the first place. Although I disliked the theatrical, goofy acting and conversing, and the exaggerated historic involvement also, I simply adored the style of this film. Such a dreamy, playful atmosphere, formed by enchanting music and creative assemblage of images.

Title: Amour
Review: When nothing else is left, there's still love. A realistic drama about growing old cruelly, in which we see the Haneke-typical subtle grimness, yet with a notable touch of positivity  constituted by Georges. His unconditional love is admirable, his final deed for Anne heroic. The nonmoving camera, silence and dusty but elegant photography make up a minimal, coherent style that aids the film well in its moral purpose.

Title: Cave of Forgotten Dreams
Review: The ancient rock art is beautiful and really induces a feeling of awe and wonder: how much are we alike and how do we differ from these early men? I did find the documentary a bit messy though. Sometimes it bored me and was difficult to follow, as if intented for specialists. The 3D was very nice at times, but mostly it annoyed me, causing my attention span to drop. Still, those wall paintings are intensely touching.

Title: The Salt of the Earth
Review: Lovely portrait of philantropist photographer Salgado's compelling life and photography. Traveling the world he captures the most terrific circumstances, demonstrating mankind's cruel nature. It's beautiful to see him increasingly focus on nature and animals later on though while keeping his otherworldly, moving style. An exemplary human being conveying the film's optimistic message: it's not too late for our planet.

Title: The Seventh Seal
Review: Beautiful depiction of people's fear and despair regarding the Black Death. I particularly like the knight who wants tangible evidence for his faith and plays chess with Death. I didn't care much for many of the humorous parts though, which interrupted the darkly poetic intensity every now and then. Also, I particularly disliked Jof perceiving the chess game, which mixed the real and the mystical in an ugly way.

Title: Before Sunrise
Review: Before Sunrise has captured the spirit of the perfect first date -given you are a philosophical slacker- without losing credibility. No person but Linklater could have done this, him being the true slacker representative who's capable of devising such authentic and interesting philosophical dialogues. I had an intense experience watching this, as if it were part of my own life. It is the ultimate slacker-romance.

Title: Land of Silence and Darkness
Review: Very touching and slightly depressing documentary about deaf-blind people which makes you realize the value of your precious senses. No fancy production, but raw, slow-paced realistic filming that shows the spleenful lives of those with no hearing and sight. Their struggle, isolation, otherworldly perception and dependency on training to at least communicate by sign language based on touch is extraordinary. Awesome.

Title: Chronicle of a Summer
Review: At first the film feels like a slightly generic, amusing documentary, but after some time it grows on you. The conversations on what were then actual social-political issues are interesting, and -more importantly- very real. Ultimately, the film seems an accurate depiction of the spirit of the age. The conclusive discussion at the end in which the interviewees take part adds to the feeling of authenticity. Neat!

Title: De grote stilte
Review: Strikes me as an unusual film in Bergman's oeuvre, but also as one of his best. Often his focus is a bit one-dimensional, on emotional interaction and character. This film adds to this a bizarre, humorous perspective -through the eyes of the young, confused Johan- vulgar eroticism and on top of that it uses the inadequate understanding of people speaking different languages in several strong ways. Great!

Title: Futurama: Into the Wild Green Yonder
Review: Has some very humorous parts in it, but overall it doesn't make much sense. Above all, the ending is horrible.

Title: Boyhood
Review: Showing barely any spectacular events, but mostly the moments in between with which life is abundantly filled, this film succeeds to capture the ghost of everyday life. Thanks to the twelve years of filming there's an undisputable natural progression of the actors that undeniably has as natural an influence on their character. This gives way for a genuine emotional involvement for the watcher. A unique masterpiece.

Title: Futurama: Bender's Game
Review: Not everyone seems to enjoy it, but I think it really lives up to the Futurama vibe of the series. This may be because it's very geeky, revolving around about Dungeons & Dragons to mock it friendly in a tongue-in-cheek way, while also using it as means to create a romantic, alternative fantasy universe in which Planet Express plays a very humorous role. Finally, the intro film of this movie is amazing. Nice film!

Title: Futurama: The Beast with a Billion Backs
Review: Although it has its qualities, including the beautifully drawn 'tentacled' planet Earth and witty humor, it lacks the warmth that is typical to Futurama and it's slightly too weird and over-the-top I guess. It's still okay, though not really good.

Title: Futurama: Bender's Big Score
Review: Great puns and high level comedy as one can expect from Futurama. It's a tad sentimental and arguably overly complicated, though also very ingenious and intelligent. In the end, it delivered.

Title: Winter Light
Review: The Bible and its teachings offer a nice romantic philosophy, but where is God in desperate times, when you really need him? Pastor Ericsson does not understand 'this silence of God' and renounces his faith. An honest depiction of a clergyman who could no longer take shelter behind fictitious stories and has to face his sinister life. Put together meticulously; certainly no short-sighted attack on Christianity.

Title: The Kid with a Bike
Review: Even though Cyril's going through a very rough patch, you can't help but feel annoyed or mad at him at times. Especially when he got really mischievous I gave up hope on him. But in a brilliant, natural way it was revealed to me that all was part of the process of grief, including seeing a father figure in the dealer guy. Samantha's love is inspiring, supporting this to be a comparatively optimistic Dardenne film.

Title: The Son
Review: Any rock processed in the Dardenne factory both keeps its roughness and shines like a diamond. Art house cinema the way it's supposed to be: without the pretentions, full of story and reality.

Title: Under the Skin
Review: Even though I loved the atmosphere and Scarlett's acting, I felt misguided mostly. Often I felt  inclined to put pieces of information together and failed to do so, because of which some actions and scenes felt random and insignificant. As a consequence my focus on experiencing the great vibe dropped, especially the poetic parts put me off because of this. Not sure who's to blame, but I feel disappointed either way.

Title: Rosetta
Review: In the harshest of circumstances it's difficult to discern between the heroic and the cruel, since then they go hand in hand. Rosetta demonstrates this, being an admirable survivor but also a deceitful friend. Poor, forsaken Rosetta is totally wrecked emotionally. Realistically acted and painful to watch. Superb film that simply breaks your heart, with an ending that might keep it close to it for some time.

Title: The Public Enemy
Review: Lots of gangster Pre-Code film are alike, but some are carried by protagonists with character. I like James Cagney as goofy and downright -which I why I love him in "The Picture Snatcher" for example- not as the big shot he's here. Furthermore, this film is a nice historical depiction of the Prohibition and has a very funny ending, but it's just a bit too plain and there's too much insignificant stuff going on.

Title: Little Caesar
Review: A movie very typical for its time that distinguishes itself slightly -in the same way Scarface does- by a great protagonist. Edward G. Robinson portrays a credible and enthralling gangster, which takes the film to another level. Still I got the feeling I've seen most of this before, so it's good, but not great. LeRoy's later "I am a Fugitive From a Chain Gang" struck me as far more authentic.

Title: The New World
Review: An epic adventure film colored in with the Malick's trademark dreamy and poetic touch, though less extreme and more coherent and concrete than usual in my opinion. With appealing veracity, grand photography and music it explores humanity and nature in a way that works on the heart and senses rather than on the brain. It makes you genuinely wonder about life in the most profound sense. It was a great experience.

Title: Nostalghia
Review: A personal philosophical inquiry steeped in Tarkovsky's awesome, mystical style in which, among other things, the thin boundaries between madness, brilliance and faith are explored. The poetic approach might take getting used to but your patience will pay off. The slow pace also allows you to thoroughly digest the beautiful photography. Great film.

Title: The General
Review: In short it consists of impressive photography, a tranquil soundtrack that reminds of Murnau and ingenious, comic use of trains in all sorts of ways. I simply loved the canon! Not as humorous as Sherlock Jr. in my opinion, but certainly the more matured movie of the two.

Title: La promesse
Review: Minimalist realism, with nothing superficial added for dramatic effect, relying entirely on the ethically bleak situations and the amazingly enacted personas. A touching story full of dilemmas in which little is black and white. This film goes as deep as films ought to go, I honestly feel guilty not giving this five stars.

Title: George Washington
Review: An interesting story from the life of young oddball George, showing his clearly congenital heroism. The production is great: well-done camera work, nicely edited colors and above all a great soundtrack that defines most of the unique atmosphere in the film that's composed of realism and mysticism. Notable scenes are the painful bathroom scene and those at the end where George runs around in his hero suit. Good stuff.

Title: Whisper of the Heart
Review: Sentimental, but sufficiently realistic, especially the dialogues. Very beautifully drawn and neatly chosen wonderful sceneries. The coming-of-age like theme works its magic nicely as well. Shizuku's authenticity feels real and was capable of affecting me. I'm not very fond of the main role of the cheesy "Take Me Home, Country Roads" song, although I did like the scene in which they play it themselves. A good film!

Title: The Umbrellas of Cherbourg
Review: Stylized by dominant use of primary colors, pleasant camera work and a moving (mostly) jazzy score, this lightly experimental musical film actually made a nice impression. Usually I despise the genre, but Demy has a touch that -despite the use of lots of candlelight romance clichés- worked for me. Stuff like the portrait-shot scene transitions, high zoom level and beautiful main song show it's very well directed.

Title: The Longest Yard
Review: Fun to watch with the family, even though it's mostly a big cliche.

Title: V for Vendetta
Review: This film covers a lot of interesting topics in a single story. Inhumane leaders and projects that remind of WWII, yet with fear-driven Christianity and controlled media mixed in. Simultaneously, it's a comic based, well done action film. A bit sentimental and cheap sometimes, but a nice watch!

Title: Cosmopolis
Review: An exploration of contemporary capitalism and how it influences our humanity. The very rich Packer nearly lives in his secured limo, has lots of meaningless sex and is obsessively trying to 'figure out the yuan'. His boundless craving for more really makes him appear android-like. I like the typical Cronenberg pseudo-realistic absurd style, however the 'cool' manner of speech and some dialogues really annoyed me.

Title: Baby Face
Review: It seems at first that whoring to achieve something rather than nothing is a good idea. Inspired by the will-to-power theory of Nietzsche, Lily climbs up all the way to the top. Here she suddenly starts to love someone, viz the first man who was able to outsmart her. Does love -despite Lily's materialistic urges- conquer all? I find much of the film to be too transparent and cliche, however Stanwyck acts greatly.

Title: The Bitter Tea of General Yen
Review: One of the most open minded Pre-Code films I've seen, in which the oriental culture is not solely ridiculed, but also given a chance to show its worth compared to Christianity. The weird dreams Megan has of Yen makes it no ordinary romance too, but a rather vulgar and unclear one. Full of practical philosophical depth and interesting characters like Jones, making this a beautiful story in a relatively unbiased way.

Title: Shanghai Express
Review: A cryptic love story between the mysterious and attractive outcast Shanghai Lily and her ex-lover dr. Harvey wrapped in an interesting adventure starring a train in the Chinese civil war. Some of the humor, mostly coming from Sam Salt, seems to rely on stereotyping the Chinese as an inferior and weird people, which reminds you of the fact you're watching a Pre-Code film. Fun to watch. With great acting by Dietrich.

Title: Three Colors: Red
Review: Shot using beautiful lighting and good narrating camera work, the film explores freedom by showing telephone tapping (privacy), the judge (sentencing) and human relationships (emotional freedom). It also centers friendship, starting with the touching encounter with Rita, followed by the gradual befriending of Pierrot. Some stuff I didn't get and seemed too symbolic and coincidental for my taste, but it's a good film.

Title: Ik ben een vluchteling
Review: A beautiful existential adventure of a man constantly in bad luck striving for the American Dream, who finds himself wronged by the legal system time after time. He takes matters into own hands and escapes from prison, turning him into a lovable hero. He then resumes his ambitions and becomes an honorable citizen, but his goodwill turns against him again. Great acting, wonderfully filmed and very depressing. Classic.

Title: Frisco Jenny
Review: After losing everything, Jenny lives to provide for her son. She is kind of a tragic hero, and I find it intriguing to see a woman have this role, considering this is a 30s movie! However, she's a mother first and a survivor second. Being able only to love remotely, she is certainly proficient in showing that love. Especially the ending shows a beautiful commitment only motherly love could offer. A pleasant watch!

Title: Sunshine
Review: Produced it seems in two distinct styles: one serene and peaceful, the other sinister and abstract,  reminding of Event Horizon. Both styles are executed very nicely, however the mixing of both sometimes stands in the way of a coherent experience. Still, it's an amazing production with perhaps some sentimentality every now and then, but a great and grand adventure overall, leaving you with a feeling of astonishment.

Title: Picture Snatcher
Review: An original idea for a film and James Cagney gives it form perfectly. While progressing from crime into a legitimate job, he really remains the boyish, sneaky (but perhaps goodhearthed) hoodlum he used to be. The film is full of oddities like the sleezy, immoral 'Graphic News', Cagney chasing a schoolgirl, people shooting recklessly, but most of all the incredible newspaper men chase at the end. Good stuff!

Title: The Beast of the City
Review: A masculine battle between cops and gangsters, who are in this film regarded as similars: reckless and caring little for justice and society. And very stylefully filmed too. Beautifully composed photography and extensive use of clever angles and slow movement of the camera to support the storytelling. It finishes off with an interesting, musical-like epic battle that emphasizes the ironic nature of the film.

Title: Manhattan Melodrama
Review: An interesting tale of friendship and ethics, while having a peek in the interesting 30s of the USA. Starting out rather clumsy, I think the movie progresses very neatly. Two friends are on different sides of the law, by which the moral value of acting by principles or by means of friendship are explored. It's actually hard to decide whether the good is one is the bad one, or the other way round.

Title: Madam Satan
Review: Not sure if all of the ridiculousness is intended, but this is some bizarre and banal comedy. Typical DeMille: carefully done sensational stuff -like the beautiful costumes on the party- serving immediate entertainment value, combined with dry and witty humor. It's very cynical, thereby challenging, mocking cultural values. There's something admirable about DeMille's ironic style that triumphs over the cheap style.

Title: Footlight Parade
Review: Being no fan of musicals or cool American businessmen, I really had a tough time getting into this film. It contains some horrible humor and annoying acting, but once you accept that, the film is actually quite creative. Especially the two shows at the end are very nice. "By a waterfall" features a beautiful, timeless piece of choreography, followed by the bizarre and innuendo filled "Honeymoon Hotel".

Title: Cleopatra
Review: An apt portrayal of who was perhaps history's earliest femme fatale. DeMille's typical grand style makes you gaze with amazement at this epos. Dancers, beatings, romance, all of which seems cheap, but there's more underneath the surface to contemplate about: is this power craving seductress evil? What can be said of this love she feels for Antony? Don't let the deceptively cheap style of the film cloud your judgment.

Title: The Sign of the Cross
Review: A well-told story of the rise of Christianity in the Roman empire. It shows beautifully the contrast between the hedonistic, self-centered Romans and the virtuous, peaceful Christians. The central example is shown through the concept of love. Marcus' love for Marcia seems little more than selfish, carnal desire, whereas her love for her faith seems to transcends that. And stylish too. This is really good.

Title: Three Colors: White
Review: After going through a tough divorce we see the tragic 'loser' Karol progress from the gutter to wealth, which appears to be the main storyline, yet we see more and more hints that suggest the significant story is about dealing with the divorce. He then tricks his ex-wife, continuing their love/hate battle. A comic drama about the fight for dominance in a relationship and its breakup. Oh, and Mikolaj is just great.

Title: The Talented Mr. Ripley
Review: Stylistically this film is very nice. It's colorful, well-shot and accompanied by some very nice jazz music. Sadly, however, the acting is really weird. It's hard to take seriously at times, as if it's deliberately very 'gay' and too 'cool'. The story starts out as an interesting case, but more and more it feels implausible, mostly due to the increasing number of lucky breaks of Tom. Fun to watch, but not great.

Title: Batman Begins
Review: To some extent the film has the Batman vibe you'd hope for, but most of it is crushed by the applied Hollywood formula. Cliche camera work and soundtrack, typical personas with oneliners we've all heard before, and the horrible character development of Ra's Al Ghul, whose cheap role in the plot is far too prominent. All in all it's nothing new: just another issue from the good ol' Hollywood press. Disappointing.

Title: The Red Circle
Review: The heist is utilized for displaying the complex, nonverbal interactions, and for showcasing the colorful, decorative, creatively shot and detailed style. The heist is shown silently and slowly paced. Melville turned genre cliches into a beautiful act. For example, you wonder who knows what, and how? There are no definite answers though, because they don't actually matter. This film is, without doubt, a masterpiece.

Title: Judex
Review: I'm difficult to please when it comes to symbolism, especially in a mystic context like this. Aesthetically it's nicely done, peaking at the ball room scene with the beautiful 'birdman'. The decoration is done nicely and some personas are fun, but the whole feels jumbled and without aim. It jumps betweeen infantile humor, Judex with his unclear intentions and role, and the insignificant crime storyline. Not so great.

Title: Le notti bianche
Review: Though at times a bit old-fashioned and cheesy considering both acting and vibe, the film's full of life and natural romance. Notable are the enchanting dance scene, where the magic blossoms tremendously between them dancing, and the snowy end scene, which is so grievously real. Throughout the film treats you with marvellous photography, carefully composed and arranged. Also, if you've read the book: watch this.

Title: Her
Review: I really enjoyed this film. It has a very appealing and easy on the eye visual style. Accompanied by a smooth and soft soundtrack this forms an accessible but fine style. The idea of the film is original, and I'd say realised very well. It avoids being too cliche, while not becoming too experimental at the same time. Ultimately it aims to make everyone -film nerds and the larger audience- happy, and does a good job.

Title: Escape from New York
Review: In the beautifully decorated prison-town Manhattan you get to experience a zombie-esque suspense, bizarre characters and weird events. The film does, however, maintain the vibe of not being ridiculously over-the-top, mostly thanks to moderation and variety. The inventive idea of Manhattan's new use, Isaac Hayes in a car with chandeliers mounted on it and Kurt Russell as the typical douchebag hero: what's not to like?

Title: Mr. Nobody
Review: Unaware of the film's long duration, I slowly died watching it. After the first 30 minutes, which were mildly enjoyable, it disappointed me for one reason after another. It's aimless and incoherent, produced in an annoying and cliche style and a horribly bad mix of romance and sci-fi. It's simply terrible in just about each and every way, I really wish I had a time machine.

Title: Blow-Up
Review: What a playful, energetic and authentic work by Antonioni. Its protagonist is oddly compelling and his charming and mischievous character is backed by creative filming like the random interruption of Thomas's photo analysis by the two girls, resulting in the flirtatious frolicking. There's a lot of beautiful shots in this film, and an interesting ending as well. Be warned though, this film does require some patience.

Title: Samurai Cop
Review: From the immediate start you just know this is going to be very, very, very bad. The movie is so bad, that I honestly don't believe it's unintentional, even though a lot of people on the web seem to disagree. It's a great laugh from time to time, but perhaps a bit much to be looking at for 96 minutes.

Title: Blue Ruin
Review: We get to follow the mysterious, sad looking guy named Dwight moving from one weird situation to another. Slowly, his story is told and his intentions are clarified. The plot turns out to be deceivingly simple, but this is used in a very original way. A quite minimalist film with great suspense accompanied by subtle, goofy humor, clean production, easy on the eyes and ears. I really like the ending too.

Title: Three Colors: Blue
Review: Beautiful shots, lively colors and the best possible character development you can hope for. Julie's personality and growth are both realistic and fascinating. Credits to Binoche for her marvellous acting! I didn't care much for the poetic use of music and the parts about the compositions though, and found the use and role of music in The Double Life Of Véronique more succesful. Nonetheless, this film is fantastic.

Title: Chasing Ice
Review: Using mainly images, this film proves beyond doubt that at least something is horribly wrong climatically. It hurts me watching this, to see proof of how bad the situation is and how quickly it worsens at the hands of mankind. It's not all depressing though. The film is visually breathtaking and the adventure of the project is well documented. Ultimately, this is a bright initiative to inform in an accessible way.

Title: The Wind Rises
Review: Probably Miyazaki's most mature film, moving beyond the typical fairylike story. It's layered and not as easy to digest as most of his earlier films. The protagonist is not a typical hero, but a realistic human being who makes questionable choices. You are also confronted with the hard nature of reality in several ways. But rest assured, it's all in the magical style we've grown so attached to. Nearly a masterpiece!

Title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
Review: This is most certainly Anderson's most mature work, in which he pulls out all the stops to fuel his fairylike and grand style. It's charming, visually stunning and versatile. Personally though, I'm just not a very big fan of this particular style, especially the humor doesn't appeal to me. It's clearly a good film, but not entirely my taste.

Title: Upstream Color
Review: Starting out with a highly creative and mysterious idea of science fiction, this movie takes you on a journey that becomes more and more spiritual. Its dreamy and colorful style add to the completeness of the experience, as does the music of which the score is composed by Shane Carruth himself. With the same authenticity and complexity as Primer, but more mature and diverse, Carruth created Upstream Color.

Title: Tropic Thunder
Review: My mood demanded over-the-top comedy, and Tropic Thunder delivered far beyond expectations. It's absurd, creative and exaggerated without being tiresome. One of the better comedies I've seen in years, certainly recommended for one of those days where nothing gets you going and you simply want to laugh.

Title: Stranger Than Fiction
Review: Will Ferrell manages okay playing a serious role, and the movie is easy to watch and fun. The concept is authentic and creative, and certainly keeps you busy during the film. I'm not too fond of all the characters though -notably the professor and the writer- and found the story quite cliche, especially with the feel-good ending and all. It's definitely a decent and fun film though.

Title: The Secret World of Arrietty
Review: As one might expect from a Ghibli film, the style and animation is beautiful. Some of the soundtrack is too, however the Japanese pop songs are more humorous than they are good. The concept of the little people is quite nice, and the story with the sick boy and especially the doll house is really inventive. At the same time, the film is a bit generic Ghibli. In the end though, I can say I've had a fun adventure.

Title: Event Horizon
Review: It starts out as a typical sci-fi film, but gradually it becomes mystically evil. The characters form a reliably typical team, including the joker, the badass practical captain and the shy doctor who's got something to hide. The production is beautiful: the ships, suits and shots in space all look great. Most importantly, it explores the limits of science in an authentic, playful way that's very enthralling.

Title: The Seventh Continent
Review: I'm absolutely in love with the style of filming. Its tranquil and slow paced, high zoomlevel style perfectly fits the daily routines and proceedings that are shown in a realistic fashion. At times it feels as if you're watching an ambient film! At some point I've got a bit impatient with it, but ultimately my attention was drawn again by the slow revelation of the dark truth behind this apparently normal family.

Title: The Man from Earth
Review: This film revolves around a remarkably original and interesting thought experiment about a caveman who has lived for 14,000 years, telling his story. The discussion is worked out well. The critical questions are those that naturally come to mind, and John's answers are sharp and clever. It's a tad exaggerated though, since in addition to his extreme survival he also got to meet lots of legends, and was Jesus himself.

Title: The Little Mermaid
Review: After getting used to some of the tedious ceremonial stuff and giggling girls -it is a fairytale after all- I kind of liked this dark and more adult adaptation of The Little Mermaid. The blue, surreal undersea palace, dreamy slowmotion scenes and the beautiful shots of glittering sea surfaces all add up to the authentic style of this film. Even though it might be just a bit too fairytalish for me it's certainly nice.

Title: Forks Over Knives
Review: Caring not for the dull production, but for its inspiring message, I was flabbergasted and enthusiastic to change my ways. However, once you read some of the critique published on the web, you feel a bit lied to. The message in this documentary may be valuable, but its proof is very unreliable and criticized severely, especially the China Study (critique by Denise Minger). I'm not so sure what to think of the whole.

Title: Food, Inc.
Review: The bio-industry -particularly in the USA- has become more extreme than many of us would've dared to imagine, ethically (for both workers and animals) and environmentally. This documentary shows the consumer the status quo, while confronting him with the influence and power he has to change things. It's nicely produced and easy to watch, and I believe it's reliable.

Title: Blue Is the Warmest Color
Review: Life will not be the same once you've had your first love, and rarely that's an easy thing to cope with. Adèle, like most of us, learns this the hard way. Relationships are difficult and love can hurt like nothing else, and it takes incredible actors to make this pain channel through the film. This movie is exceptionally realistic: the dialogues, flirting, plot, everything's right. I consider this a masterpiece.

Title: Withnail & I
Review: It took me some time to grow into it, but I had a good time watching this movie. The characters are cartoony and comicly exaggerated, although there are times the jokes don't work too well. Uncle Monty adds a necessary dimension to the fun and completes the character base. A beautifully ridiculous cult movie which won't be enjoyed by everyone, but is worth checking out on a lazy Sunday.

Title: This Is Spinal Tap
Review: It was fun to watch, but I think a lot of it was  overdone in a way that didn't suit me. The music is very cool though, and the bearded guy is definitely hilarious.

Title: Dallas Buyers Club
Review: It's certainly an inspirational story, to see an HIV carrying, relentless redneck turn his world view inside out after his diagnosis, becoming an active fighter for AIDS patients. The film has a nice balance of drama and entertainment, and is quite accessible to watch. I enjoyed it!

Title: Our Daily Bread
Review: An ambient documentary about the modern agricultural industry. There's not a single spoken word in it, neither is there music. It uses only beautiful images and environmental sounds. It doesn't take an obvious stand, but seems to have the intent to show the industry as objective as possible. Its style is clean and aesthetically pleasing, its message unspoken and ambiguous, but inspiring.

Title: Meaning of Robots
Review: It's about a fat, bearded guy obsessed with building robots with 'fuckable holes' and genitalia. Do I need to say more?

Title: La Pointe Courte
Review: The film consists of two stories in the idyllic La Pointe Courte: a struggling married couple, whose story is told in a poetic and experimental (for the time) form, and the townspeople -chiefly the fishermen- fighting for their survival, a story that's told with careful realism. It's beautifully shot and there's some great acting. The film is charming, real and evokes feelings of nostalgia. It's simply beautiful.

Title: Taken
Review: Liam Neeson is Steven Seagal in this over-the-top, well-produced action movie. It has a very high tempo with lots of entertaining violence, bad racial stereotyping and the American action hero: a typical action movie? Yes and no. It looks the same, but at times it seems cynical and self-deprecating. Also, the rescue of his daughter and fighting the sex slave trade might feel satisfying even to innocent house moms.

Title: Mind Game
Review: A playful, surreal celebration of life. Sometimes it's nostalgic and touching, then -mockingly?- superficial in its display of violence and the carnal -boobs and guns!-, and throughout it's bizarre and original. Stylistically, it is stunning and continuously refreshing, which by itself makes it enthralling enough to watch. Finally: this is not typical anime. Even if you're no anime fan, you might want to try it.

Title: Duin
Review: I like cult, but this one crosses the line. Most of this film was randomly stupid -a floating laughing baron?- inconsistent and nonsensical. The idea of evolved creatures folding space was okay, but why the hell does it require 'spice'? Also, this idea was barely paid any attention. Instead, the film focused on the politics of the Universe. So many things annoyed me, it's just bad. The worms were pretty cool though.

Title: Een Andalusische hond
Review: Progressive and courageous, but also pretentious and boring. I can imagine its influence and possibly shocking character at the time, but nonetheless it fails its primary purpose to captivate me.

Title: The Tree of Life
Review: At first I enjoyed the marvellous visuals, both the rendered and shot images. The soundtrack is very beautiful and even the poetry had its moments. This, however, only amused me for about ninety minutes. After that, its fragmented and boring plot, randomly nonsensical poetry and lack of aim/tension made me wish for the film to end for an hour long. I think Malick's poetry is not for me.

Title: The Wrestler
Review: More than being just the story of a wrestler facing retirement, this is about becoming old and facing the choices you made in life. Even though the film has a few easy sentiments that make it more accessible, they don't feel cheap, they actually touched me. Rourke acts very well, and is perfectly cut for the role.  Life's a bitch, and then you die, so why not in the glamerous world you understand.

Title: Love in the Afternoon
Review: Starring Chloe, a respectable, overtly manipulative femme fatale, and Frédéric, a starry-eyed, married bourgeois who is targeted by Chloe's seductive powers. His decency protects him initially, but eventually the love for his wife is put to the test. Surprisingly and beautifully, it triumphs. Leave it to Rohmer to depict interesting and real human beings, their subtle behavioral characteristics and complex stories.

Title: Adam
Review: It's okay pastime, but sadly overly enumerative when it comes to demonstrating the life of an Asperger. The enacted symptoms are typical and prevalent, but feel copy/pasted, as if all of them absolutely must be shown. Make all of them very severe and Adam becomes a living schoolbook definition. The attempt to pay attention to autism is appreciated, but it's too linear and overdone.

Title: Lars and the Real Girl
Review: A bit effusive, but then again it is an accessible fun film intended for the whole family. There's some charm to it all, but I wouldn't consider it special in any way.

Title: Cube
Review: The acting is bad, the characters are even worse and it is full of tricks and cliches. The concept is interesting though, and it has some fun mathematical details.

Title: Claire's Knee
Review: This film is about playing games of seduction, covered up with theories that speak of idealistic, slightly platonic love. The young Laura seems well aware of this internal struggle, while one might doubt if Jerome does. He seems blinded and insincere at times, yet heartfelt and true at others. Again, Rohmer leaves you with genuine questions, not with simple closure. And did I mention the beautiful Swedish scenery?

Title: Herfstsonate
Review: Once again Bergman explores family relationships with a big zoomlevel on the psyches involved. Realistic acting, truthful characters and emotionally complex situations result into this masterpiece of cinema. This film, being very intense, surprises you with a relatively sober ending that actually suits it perfectly.

Title: Antichrist
Review: The film does not aim for complete experimentalism, yet toys around recklessly with vague symbols and mostly nonsensical and redundantly sexual mysticism, that was interesting at times but mostly boring and unsuccesful. I did enjoy the style of filming and most of the acting, but it didn't exactly save the film as a whole.

Title: Late Spring
Review: At first it was a bit boring to me, and I struggled with the inexplicable permanent smile on Noriko's face. After some time I got used to this Asian style of emotions though and feel like I've learned something about Japanese culture. The photography in the film is amazing. It's incredible how many parallell lines can be found in just about every shot: it's wonderfully symmetrical. This is clean, real cinema.

Title: Spring Breakers
Review: On the surface it seems to be a mainstream film with hot partying people at Spring Break, a ridiculously funny gangster James Franco, guns and sex. This is just a disguise though, because it's really a full-blown bizarre cult film, carrying an existentialist question: 'how do I live a satisfying life?'. Wrap all this up in an uncanny dreamy atmosphere -both visually and musically- and you have an incredible movie.

Title: Europa Report
Review: You can tell a lot of effort has been put into making this film, which explains its authenticity. Sadly though I didn't enjoy much of this style, and often I was a bit bored or didn't think the acting is very convincing. Sometimes, however, the acting is very convincing and the visuals can be really stunning. On the whole, the film was okay, but not much more than that.

Title: Time of the Wolf
Review: A survival movie on the surface, but a psychological experiment at the core. In an interesting way it explores human behaviour in an apocalyptic setting, and does so quite realistically. This being my first Haneke, I was especially pleased with the images, which vary from dark, foggy and gray to light and neutral, always carrying some serenity over them, regardless of the depressing content they depict. I liked it.

Title: Is the Man Who Is Tall Happy?
Review: Not knowing Chomsky well, this was a nice introduction to his views and to him as a person. He strikes me as an authentic and respectful thinker, not just the usual academic void wrapped in a person. The animations were okay, often adjusting well to the discussion. Parts of the conversation are a bit repetitive, but this causes the tough material to become more accessible. Gondry's playful style adds to this as well.

Title: La collectionneuse
Review: The mechanics of the sophisticated cat-and-mouse game between two manipulators are revealed most beautifully in this film. Haydée uses her charms and seductive skills, while Adrien devises his plans rationally. Once again Rohmer knows how to fill a simple sequence of plain events with a fundamental dynamic between human beings, resulting in this complex and real piece of cinema, that actually shows you life.

Title: Short Term 12
Review: With a remarkable balance between accessibility and veracity, this film seeks emotional depth while also keeping things hopeful and light. The comedy is fun and lighthearted - even a bit childish, and forms a big part of the authentic style of the film. However, a few times I thought the comedy impairs the plausibility. I enjoyed this film, and conclude by giving special credits to the actors of Marcus and Grace.

Title: The Holy Mountain
Review: At first I didn't take the film too seriously, but I ended up enjoying more of it than just the weirdly dressed toads, fecal inhalation and limbless people. The film has a wonderfully colorful setting -by itself a reason to watch the film- which accompanies the bizarre, authentic humor. Some stuff is pretty gross, but it's not cheap entertainment. In a weird way the film seems pretentious, but is actually sincere.

Title: Sans Soleil
Review: This film gives you a subtly experimental, cultural trip, disguised as a -actually informative- documentary with a philosophical, poetic voice over. It feels intimate, almost personal, and there are moments I emphathized, yet there was always an odd, alienating and slightly surreal feel present. Remarkably, this film doesn't seem to aim for anything, though it eventually seems to denote the painful essence of being.

Title: Sherlock Jr.
Review: This certainly is a surprisingly progressive and authentically funny movie, which hardly feels dated. It's full of ingenious and resourceful tricks. Particularly notable is obviously Keaton's long dream in the cinema in which one funny situation follows the other, each different from the last in style. It's true craftmanship. On top of it all the movie is produced charmingly, including pleasantly accompanying music.

Title: My Night at Maud's
Review: The Christian Jean-Louis struggles in a world that seems unfathomably determined by fate and full of temptation. Free-spirited Maud challenges his mental strength by tempting him with the most primitive weapon she possesses. This film is full of interesting philosophical conversations - which do sometimes carry on a bit too long and thorough - and truthfully depicted, ambiguous characters, enacted plain and real.

Title: Up
Review: Shown to us is the dramatic nature of life through the eyes of Mr. Fredericksen, and by contrast the infantile and eupeptic experience of Russell. The animation is fantastic: not only is the rendering incredible, but the degree of detail in which for example facial expressions are done really touched me in a way Disney hasn't for a long time. I enjoyed this movie, and wish I could've seen it as a child.

Title: A Prophet
Review: Malik, who keeps up an appearance of being pushed around and soft, is actually the subtle master of dialogue and manipulation, arranging deals with all of the opposing groups. The way this is shown in the film strikes me as realistic and innovative. It is a bit long though and might be a bit too 'prisony' for me on the whole, that is it doesn't entirely escape the cliches of the genre. Certainly a good film though.

Title: Le beau Serge
Review: The quiet village life that Jacques expects to return to turns out to have evolved into a dark, bestial society. Appearances fool him at first, but soon his trust is put even more to the test. The poor village life has turned his old friend Serge, among others, into an envious and jealous human being. This film shows the dark side of humanity that is governed by our most primal emotions, disguised in complexity.

Title: Prisoners
Review: It is smoothly produced and easy to watch, which makes it an appealing way to kill time, but I'm afraid it's not that special. It's full of Hollywood cliches and plays with the mind in a way we've seen a million times before. Some writing is actually done pretty well, including clever backreferences and perhaps slight originality, but ultimately I feel betrayed, as if I've watched yet another American thriller movie.

Title: Sucker Punch
Review: I usually don't watch action films with a flashy character, but was persuaded by a friend to watch this one anyway. And you know, if you close your eyes to some cliche acting and directing this movie actually has an interesting, authentic style. Also, the way the movie ends has some nice ring to it, even though the message is a bit over the top. Accompanied by a nice soundtrack, I had a quite good time watching this.

Title: The Truman Show
Review: At first, it all seems like a nicely done TV show, but slowly, the mystery is unraveled and ethical questions arise. It's nice how Christoph defends his opinion by stating to have put Truman inside a safer world than any of us, and how many people seem to agree. Also, I like the details through which Truman finds out about his actual purpose in life. This movie certainly is special, I really enjoyed it.

Title: Als in een donkere spiegel
Review: A painfully realistic film showing the double faced nature of man, shown mostly through the family dynamics in this film. And then I haven't mentioned the main subject in the film, which obviously is poor Karin and her mental illness. She acts very well, and I think the illness is displayed truthfully in this film. To top it all off there's the beautiful location and photography. I love this film!

Title: La dolce vita
Review: You can clearly feel Fellini's film making mastery throughout the entire film: great shots, interesting dialogue, an authentic soundtrack and an adventure relying on nothing cheap and easy. I did not enjoy the ending though, which is obiously a big shame. I think it takes things too far. The explicit, aggressive turn Marcello felt exaggerated and stylistically inconsistent to me, too shocking for a film this subtle.

Title: Little Fugitive
Review: This movie makes you experience the adventurous life of a child again. It is charming, authentic and fun. The visual style is stunning in its own, independent way, and Joey is just a lovely kid. I love this movie, it's great.

Title: Double Indemnity
Review: Not too much of a film noir fan, I feared a typical plot, with cliche characters wearing rain coats and hats, or walking on high heels and smoking a cigarette. I was right about those genre characteristics, but wrong about them being tiresome. The plot is very well thought through and not completely unambiguous. The characters are very well portrayed and the suspense is entertaining. I'm suprised by the quality!

Title: The Bakery Girl of Monceau
Review: Dreams do come true at times, and sometimes stories don't end too well for everyone. This tale is raw and real, it hurts to see the bestial truth of the mechanics of love, but it makes perfect sense. The ending is a bit rushed, which I both like and dislike. It's a very nice short either way.

Title: Suzanne's Career
Review: It's real, insightful and complete. The main characters are interesting and realistic, and their dynamic is complex and beautiful. The ultimate moral teaching of the film tops it all off. This is a style that I can endure for hours!

Title: Amer
Review: Fluctuating between abstract eroticism and surreal, paranoid mysticism, this film certainly is weird. You seem to be experiencing life through the eyes of Ana, who has a ruptured sense of reality. Her extremely perceptive senses are brilliantly represented by the intense lighting and 'windy', erotic sounds. I'd say the film has a very authentic style overall, with a high zoom level and lots of detail. I loved it!

Title: Jules and Jim
Review: Beautiful movie about friendship and love. It has a slightly bizarre touch, but stays natural and clean in style. Even though I sometimes had difficulty adjusting my expectations between realism and poetry, the film did a marvellous job. Jules, Jim and Catherine are very interesting characters, especially some dialogues are particularly enthralling.

Title: The Animatrix
Directors: Peter Chung,Andy Jones,Yoshiaki Kawajiri,Takeshi Koike,Mahiro Maeda,Kôji Morimoto,Shinichiro Watanabe

Title: The Invention of Lying
Review: I like how some scenarios work out, especially the religious aspect and the egomaniacal, manipulative misuse of his ability to lie. Ultimately however, it is wrapped in a cliche Hollywood formula, which ruins the movie for me. There's the girl, the happy ending you can see coming from miles ahead and not to forget the typical feel-good, smooth production. I had some fun, but that's it.

Title: Waterschapsheuvel
Review: A magnificent, primal adventure confronting us with the most basic natural phenomena in life: freedom, love and friendship, death. Accessible to children as well - partly because of the obvious distinction between good and bad - though a bit cruel, but that's also honest and educational, since life is like that. Furthermore there's the beautiful style in both drawing and music, making this film an all-round success.

Title: Network
Review: Even though I enjoyed the style and theme, I found the film exaggerating in both plot - the sudden madness of Beale - and acting - Diane's enthusiasm. I just didn't buy it. At the end it really touched me though with insightful monologues by Beale and Jensen. Sadly however, it ends with yet another example of exorbitance. It's a nice movie with an interesting, authentic theme, but some stuff just doesn't work for me.

Title: World on a Wire
Review: A visually stunning sci-fi film with the philosophical richness a la Solyaris, an existential crisis that I felt in Naked Lunch and somewhat poetic and exaggeratedly beautiful, classy women that reminds of Godard. It has all that and more: a cat and mouse game with the creator, a mysterious atmosphere that challenges the mind, and Plato put to practice. This film is of the highest possible level, a masterpiece.

Title: Pretty Bird
Review: Despite its exaggerated nature, I really enjoyed this film. As usual Paul Giamatti performs wonderfully, and the other actors are reasonably enjoyable as well. The soundtrack is amazing and really sets an authentic mood for the film. The comedy is very good at times, and I must say I also enjoyed the story. I don't see why this film seems so unliked, because I really like it.

Title: Metropolis
